decisions.title: Canonical HTTP route parameter spelling
decisions.gist: Choose how named and catch-all route segments are written in Jet source.
decisions.lesson:
A router compares an incoming URL path with registered patterns. A literal segment matches itself. A named parameter captures one segment. A catch-all captures the remaining segments.

Jet String literals already give braces a language meaning. In "/users/{id}", Jet evaluates `id` and inserts its value. Doubling the braces, as in "/users/{{id}}", produces literal braces at runtime.

This creates two layers. Jet first builds a String. The router then reads that String as a route pattern. A route marker must survive the first layer unchanged.

The spelling affects ordinary source, generated routes, diagnostics, logs, and conflict detection. Two accepted spellings would also create two names for one routing mechanism.

For example, a one-segment parameter might capture `42` from `/users/42`. A final catch-all might capture `css/site.css` from `/assets/css/site.css`.

Beginners need one pattern they can copy directly. Experts need stable canonical patterns for registration conflicts, middleware metadata, access logs, and audits.
decisions.story: Nia adds tenant routes to a service and copies the ratified `/users/{id}` example. Jet treats `id` as String interpolation, so her route depends on a value instead of declaring a parameter.
decisions.detail: This amends only the route-pattern spelling in D-HTTP-SERVER2=A. Its one Router, Handler composition, precedence, decoding, conflict, middleware, lifecycle, and safety laws remain unchanged. Every option supplies one canonical source form and rejects the others with a migration diagnostic. No compatibility alias or second router is allowed.

options.name: Colon parameter and named star catch-all
options.detail: Write `:name` for one segment and final `*name` for the remainder. Both markers survive ordinary Jet Strings unchanged, and the form extends the router's current colon mechanism.
options.technical: A pattern segment exactly matching `:name` captures one decoded segment. A final segment exactly matching `*name` captures zero or more remaining decoded segments joined by `/`. Names use `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and must be unique. Literal segments beginning with either marker use normal URL percent encoding. Static beats parameter beats catch-all, as already ratified. Canonical route metadata preserves `:name` and `*name`. Bare final `*`, `{name}`, `{*name}`, and doubled-brace source forms are rejected with a diagnostic naming the canonical spelling. Existing bare `*` receives a source-migration diagnostic to `*wildcard`; it is not an alias. No new Router type, route builder, or compiler interpolation exception is added.

options.name: Doubled braces in Jet source
options.detail: Keep brace patterns in the runtime router, but require doubled braces in every Jet String literal. The source and displayed runtime pattern differ, which adds ceremony and copy-paste traps.
options.technical: Jet source uses `{{` and `}}` to emit literal braces. The router receives `{name}` or `{*name}` and retains D-HTTP-SERVER2's original grammar. Dynamically produced Strings must also contain those runtime braces. Diagnostics must distinguish Jet interpolation errors from router-pattern errors. Colon and star-prefix forms are rejected; no aliases are retained.

options.name: Structured route segments
options.detail: Build a typed Route from literal, parameter, and catch-all segments. This removes String ambiguity, but makes the beginner path verbose and adds another public construction surface.
options.technical: Router registration accepts only `Route`. `Route.path` receives a sequence of `Literal`, `Param`, and final `CatchAll` values, validates names, and owns canonical display. String patterns are retired. This adds public values and builders but no second matching engine.
options.code:
route :: http.Route.path([
  .Literal("orgs"), .Param("org"),
  .Literal("repos"), .Param("repo")
+])?
router.get(route, show_repo)

comparisons.note: Express uses colon-prefixed named segments, so ordinary JavaScript Strings carry route markers without another escape layer.
Modern ServeMux uses braces, but ordinary Go String literals do not interpolate braces. Jet's String layer changes that usability tradeoff.
Axum also uses braces inside non-interpolating Rust String literals. Its source spelling therefore reaches the router unchanged.

recommendation.why: A keeps ordinary route registration short, survives Jet interpolation unchanged, and evolves the existing colon matcher into one fully named route grammar. Beginners copy the displayed source directly. Experts get stable named templates.

whyNot.reason: B makes every brace route look different in source and runtime metadata. Examples copied from logs or other tools require a Jet-specific doubling step.
C replaces a readable path with a segment construction API. It adds public types and ceremony without improving the single matching engine's safety or determinism.

recommendation.tradeoff: A reserves colon-prefixed and star-prefixed pattern segments. Literal path segments with those prefixes must use standard percent encoding, and current bare `*` routes require a named migration.

decisions.checkInstructions: Amend D-HTTP-SERVER2's exact route law without changing its matching or safety rules. Record the route markers in Syntax.rs with this decision ID and update syntax-decisions.md. Prove literal, parameter, named catch-all, percent-encoded sigils, duplicate names, conflicts, precedence, logs, migration diagnostics, and AOT/dev parity. Retain one Router and no aliases.

decisions.title: Typed HTTP error for unsupported build targets
decisions.gist: Choose how HTTP reports an operation that the compiled target cannot provide.
decisions.lesson:
A build target is the operating environment selected when compiling a program. Some targets provide network sockets and listeners. Others deliberately omit one or both capabilities.

An unsupported-target error means the compiled environment cannot perform an operation at all. It differs from a timeout, refused connection, permission failure, or exhausted resource on a target that supports the operation.

Jet's `HttpError` is a closed enum. Callers can handle every named case, and a new case changes exhaustive matching. D-HTTP-CORE2 therefore listed its variants exactly.

A later ruling requires unavailable listener operations to return typed `UnsupportedTarget`. That name is absent from the exact list, so both rulings cannot be implemented literally without an amendment.

A payload can identify which HTTP operation was unavailable. A String payload is less precise because spelling, backend details, and future values are not checked by the compiler.

Beginners normally propagate the error with `?` and receive stable guidance. Experts may match the operation to disable a server, select another deployment target, or record an audit fact.
decisions.story: Mateo cross-compiles one service for Linux and WASI. Client code is allowed by one deployment, but listener creation is unavailable in another, and he needs a stable typed branch before any handler starts.
decisions.detail: This decision reconciles D-HTTP-CORE2=A with D-DEP-HTTP2=B. It changes only the shared closed error law for statically unavailable HTTP socket capabilities. All clients, servers, shortcuts, routers, middleware, tests, AOT builds, and dev execution continue using one `core.http.HttpError`.

options.name: UnsupportedTarget with a closed HTTP operation
options.detail: Add one exact variant carrying a typed operation. Callers can distinguish client connection, server binding, and serving an existing listener without parsing text.
options.technical: Amend the exact D-HTTP-CORE2 list with `UnsupportedTarget { operation: HttpOperation }`. `HttpOperation` is exactly `ClientConnect`, `ServerBind`, and `ServeListener`. Return this variant only when Jet's compile-target capability matrix says the requested operation cannot exist. Return it before DNS, connect, bind, accept, handler execution, or other observable I/O. Runtime refusal remains `Connect`, runtime I/O failure remains `Io`, exhaustion remains `ResourceUnavailable`, cancellation remains `Cancelled`, and protocol mismatch remains `Protocol`. Unsupported HTTP versions or encodings never use this variant. Display and diagnostics name the public operation and say the build target lacks it. They expose no backend prose or arbitrary target String. The target remains available through normal build and audit facts.

options.name: Payload-free UnsupportedTarget
options.detail: Add a unit variant with the required name. It is compact, but shared helpers and audits cannot tell which unavailable operation produced it.
options.technical: Amend the list with only `UnsupportedTarget`. Every statically absent HTTP socket capability returns the same value. Callers infer the operation from call-site context. Runtime failures keep their existing variants. No target or backend String is exposed.

options.name: Reuse ResourceUnavailable
options.detail: Keep the existing closed list and classify a missing target capability as an unavailable resource. This avoids enum growth but erases the difference between impossible and temporarily exhausted.
options.technical: Return `ResourceUnavailable { resource: .NetworkListener }` or `.NetworkSocket` for both compile-target absence and runtime exhaustion. This requires typed resource values but adds no `UnsupportedTarget` variant. D-DEP-HTTP2's explicit error name would be amended away.

comparisons.note: Rust has `ErrorKind::Unsupported`, but the operation usually remains call-site context rather than a typed payload.
WASI worlds declare imported capabilities. A component without incoming socket support cannot create a listener merely by retrying at runtime.
comparisons.code: // build world omits incoming-handler and TCP listener authority

recommendation.why: A satisfies the later typed-error requirement while preserving one closed shared error tree. Its closed operation payload distinguishes deployment capability from transient failure without exposing backend text.

whyNot.reason: B gives experts no typed operation fact when errors cross helper, task, or audit boundaries. Call-site inference is lost once the value is forwarded.
C contradicts the ratified `UnsupportedTarget` requirement and merges permanent target absence with temporary resource pressure. Those cases require different recovery.

recommendation.tradeoff: A adds one `HttpError` variant and one three-case enum. Exhaustive matches must handle it, which is the intended visible cost of accurately extending a closed error contract.

decisions.checkInstructions: Amend D-HTTP-CORE2's exact variant list and D-DEP-HTTP2's target rule together. Prove all three operations return before side effects on unsupported targets. Prove supported-target refusal, I/O, exhaustion, cancellation, protocol, and encoding cases retain their existing variants. Verify stable redacted Display, diagnostics, exhaustive matching, AOT/dev parity, and no backend String or fallback.

decisions.title: Target profile surface
decisions.gist: Choose where embedded and freestanding target profiles are declared and selected.
decisions.story: Tess writes hosted CLIs most days, then firmware for a sensor board. Hosted hello-world stays zero ceremony; board builds expose every target assumption.
decisions.inWild: module board.sensor_v1 { target: embedded.arm.cortex_m4 }

options.name: Typed profile module selected by `targets:`
options.detail: Profiles are Jet modules with typed fields; packages select them through existing targets. Hosted single-file programs never mention profiles.
options.code:
module board.sensor_v1 { target: embedded.arm.cortex_m4 }
targets: { firmware: { profile: board.sensor_v1 } }

options.name: All profile data in `pkg.jet`
options.detail: Centralizes build data, harder to reuse and review large board profiles as source modules.
options.code: targets: { firmware: { target: embedded.arm.cortex_m4 } }

options.name: CLI-selected board files
options.detail: Good for vendor imports, less visible source provenance.
options.code: jet build src/main.jet --target-profile boards/sensor_v1.jet

comparisons.note: Target JSON plus linker scripts work, but Jet should validate before codegen.

decisions.title: Target memory regions
decisions.gist: Choose how memory regions and units are written and validated.
decisions.story: Jules has flash, SRAM, and MMIO windows. Jet should catch overflow or MMIO outside declared regions before generated Rust exists.
decisions.inWild: memory: board.memory({ flash: { origin: 0x0800_0000, size: 512.kib } })

options.name: Named regions with typed units
options.detail: Profiles use named regions with origin, size, access, and kind; sizes use distinct units and addresses stay numeric.
options.code: memory: board.memory({ flash: { origin: 0x0800_0000, size: 512.kib, access: .rx } })

options.name: Linker-section-first memory
options.detail: Matches linker thinking, hides hardware layout from MMIO and audit checks.
options.code: memory: board.sections({ text: { at: 0x0800_0000, max: 384.kib } })

options.name: Imported vendor memory map
options.detail: Useful for large boards, should not be the only authoring path.
options.code: memory: board.import("vendor/stm32f4.svd")

comparisons.note: MEMORY blocks name origin and length; Jet should type-check earlier.

decisions.title: Linker provenance
decisions.gist: Choose how linker scripts are sourced, generated, and overridden.
decisions.story: Priya builds two boards. One can use Jet-generated linker input; one must consume a vendor script. Audit must show exactly which path happened.
decisions.inWild: linker: board.linker.generated

options.name: Generated by default, hashed file override
options.detail: Jet generates linker input from typed profile facts; expert override uses explicit hashed file and appears in audit.
options.code:
linker: board.linker.generated
linker: board.linker.file("vendor/memory.x", hash: "sha256:abc123")

options.name: User linker file required
options.detail: Exposes provenance but duplicates typed memory facts.
options.code: linker: board.linker.file("memory.x", hash: "sha256:abc123")

options.name: Toolchain-provided linker policy
options.detail: Convenient, but hides board assumptions from source review.
options.code: linker: board.linker.toolchain_default

comparisons.note: Build scripts can own linker args; Jet should make source visible to dossier/audit.

decisions.title: Allocator and panic policy
decisions.gist: Choose how freestanding allocator and panic behavior are declared.
decisions.story: Mateo writes boot firmware with no heap while another board uses a fixed arena. Jet should reject accidental heap use and make panic behavior explicit.
decisions.inWild: allocator: board.allocator.fixed(region: .ram, size: 32.kib)

options.name: Typed profile fields
options.detail: `allocator` and `panic` are required freestanding profile facts; hosted defaults stay hidden. Sema rejects unavailable Core APIs from these facts.
options.code:
allocator: board.allocator.none
panic: board.panic.abort

options.name: Package target policy only
options.detail: Compact, less reusable across board modules.
options.code: targets: { firmware: { allocator: none, panic: abort } }

options.name: Source markers on entry functions
options.detail: Localizes policy but mixes build target facts into ordinary code.

comparisons.note: Panic handlers are special items; Jet should expose typed target facts.

decisions.title: Target audit report
decisions.gist: Choose the shape of the target-profile audit report.
decisions.story: Hana sends firmware to a lab. They need memory layout, linker source, allocator, panic policy, unavailable Core APIs, and unsafe/MMIO regions in one stable artifact.
decisions.inWild: jet dossier target firmware --json > target-audit.json

options.name: `jet dossier target` plus build artifact
options.detail: Canonical human/machine view is a dossier lens, and builds also write the same JSON into `.jet/` for CI archives.
options.code:
jet dossier target firmware
jet dossier target firmware --json > target-audit.json

options.name: Build artifact only
options.detail: Stable for CI, less discoverable during planning/debugging.
options.code: cat .jet/audit/firmware.target.json

options.name: Command output only
options.detail: Visible, weak for archives and tooling.
options.code: jet build firmware --audit

comparisons.note: Machine-readable build facts are useful; Jet target safety facts should be first-class.

decisions.title: Canonical binary interchange format for core.encoding
decisions.gist: Which single binary serialization format Jet ships beside json/toml/yaml/csv.
decisions.explainer: A: standardization plus a specified deterministic form (hashing/signing/content-addressing all want stable bytes) outweighs MessagePack’s ecosystem edge; one format keeps I8.
decisions.story: Marco's game syncs replay state between a Jet server and clients 60 times a second. JSON is the only interchange format Jet has, so he pays text encode/parse on every tick and his packets are 3x larger than needed. He needs one blessed binary format that works through the same @[Codable] derive — not a menu of five.

options.name: CBOR (RFC 8949)
options.detail: IETF standard with a deterministic-encoding profile (stable bytes for hashing/signing — pairs with crypto.seal and content-addressed stores), native binary strings, and a clean extension model. Same parse/to_string/decode<T> verbs as every other codec.
options.code:
use core.encoding.cbor as cbor

bytes :: cbor.to_bytes(tick)              // [U8], ~1/3 the JSON size
back :: cbor.decode<Tick>(bytes)?

// deterministic profile: same value → same bytes, always
hash :: crypto.sha256(cbor.to_bytes_canonical(tick))

options.name: MessagePack
options.detail: The most popular binary format by ecosystem (Redis, Fluentd, many game stacks). Slightly tighter encoding than CBOR in common cases; no IETF standard, no canonical-form spec — deterministic bytes for hashing would be Jet-invented.
options.code:
use core.encoding.msgpack as msgpack

bytes :: msgpack.to_bytes(tick)
back :: msgpack.decode<Tick>(bytes)?

options.name: Ship both
options.detail: Maximum interop, but two mechanisms for one semantic job — exactly what I8 rejects. Every API that accepts one must document why not the other, forever.
options.code:
use core.encoding.cbor as cbor
use core.encoding.msgpack as msgpack   // which one does your team use? both, eventually

options.name: Decline binary interchange for now
options.detail: JSON stays the only interchange. Games, caches, and IPC keep paying text overhead or hand-rolling formats — the gap every systems language fills in year one.
options.code: // status quo: json.to_string(tick) on a 60Hz loop

comparisons.note: stdlib ships encoding/gob (Go-only) — everyone actually uses CBOR or msgpack third-party; shipping neither pushed the ecosystem off-stdlib.
Codable has JSON + plist only; binary interchange is a long-standing community complaint.
comparisons.code: JSONEncoder() // or a third-party CBOR encoder

comparisons.note: CBOR is the substrate for COSE signing/encryption and WebAuthn — standards momentum is behind it.

decisions.title: Encoding XML and streaming codecs
decisions.gist: Choose how XML and large-file streaming join core.encoding.
decisions.explainer: Best hybrid: beginner whole-value APIs and expert bounded-memory streaming share one codec model.
decisions.story: Priya ingests a 20 GB vendor feed. Loading all JSON/XML into Data first is not acceptable; she needs pull parsing, typed decode, and namespace-correct XML without a second serialization model.
decisions.inWild:
use core.encoding.json as json

all :: json.parse(files.read("huge.json")?)?  // memory cliff
decisions.detail: Hybrid review 2026-07-07: recommended option combines the beginner/default path with expert control where that preserves one semantic mechanism. Best hybrid: beginner whole-value APIs and expert bounded-memory streaming share one codec model.

options.name: Hybrid: same codec modules, tree and stream modes (recommended)
options.detail: Every codec module keeps one adapter identity: parse/to_string/decode<T> for whole values and reader/writer event streams for large inputs. XML, JSONL, canonical JSON, and CBOR all flow through Data/DataTree and Codable, so streaming is a mode of the same codec, not a second library.
options.code:
doc :: xml.parse(input)?
item :: xml.decode<Item>(input)?

reader :: json.reader(file)?
loop ev in reader.events() { handle(ev) }
writer :: cbor.writer(out, canonical: true)?

options.name: Separate core.stream_encoding module
options.detail: Streaming codecs live away from normal codecs. Clear boundary, but splits one format into two places.
options.code: use core.stream_encoding.json as jsons

options.name: Tree-only codecs
options.detail: All formats parse to Data/DataTree first. Simpler surface, but fails large files and server streaming.
options.code: data :: xml.parse(input)?

comparisons.note: encoding/json Decoder streams tokens; XML decoder handles namespaces.
serde has one data model with streaming backends; Jet should keep the same one-mechanism shape.

decisions.title: Public streaming encoding surface
decisions.gist: Choose exactly how programs read and write encoded data without loading the whole document.
decisions.explainer:
Ratified D-ENCSTREAM1=A fixes the architecture, not this public spelling: every codec stays in core.encoding.<format>; whole-value and stream modes share Data/DataTree and Codable; streaming is one mode of the same adapter. This ballot adds no language syntax and does not create a second codec family. Existing parse/to_string/encode/decode and the shipped json.events(Data)->String path transcript remain unchanged under release policy. Pull events exist only through json.reader and use DataEvent. Any future json.events rename or return-type change requires an edition-migration decision with source rewrite, deprecation window, and old-edition behavior; no return-type-only overload exists (I8).

Canonical namespaces: shared EncodingLimits, EncodingError, EncodingCause, EncodingFormat, EncodingErrorKind, DataEvent, and Data live only in core.encoding and are referenced through `use core.encoding as encoding`. Format handles and format-only options/events live only in core.encoding.json, .jsonl, .csv, .xml, and .cbor and are referenced through those aliases. FileReader/FileWriter remain core.files types; no duplicate re-exports exist.

Option A exact declarations are public opaque JSONReader/JSONWriter, JSONLReader/JSONLWriter, CSVReader/CSVWriter, and CBORReader/CBORWriter structs with private fields; none derives Codable, Copy, or Clone. XMLReader/XMLWriter exist only if D-ENCXML1 first supplies the exact conditional schema described below. Every reader declares `pub fn next(&self) -> Item? ? encoding.EncodingError`. Every writer declares `pub fn write(&self, item: Item) -> Void ? encoding.EncodingError`, `pub fn flush(&self) -> Void ? encoding.EncodingError`, and `pub fn finish(&self) -> Void ? encoding.EncodingError`. `&self` is the exact edit capability because each call advances state; callers keep handles in changeable bindings. Each format exports `reader(input: ^files.FileReader, limits: encoding.EncodingLimits = encoding.EncodingLimits.safe()) -> Reader ? encoding.EncodingError` and `writer(output: ^files.FileWriter, limits: encoding.EncodingLimits = encoding.EncodingLimits.safe()) -> Writer ? encoding.EncodingError`; json.writer alone adds `canonical: Bool = false`. Constructor calls consume handles with ^ per D-MEM1. Invalid limits or setup IO return EncodingError and the consumed handle closes by RAII; no failed constructor leaks or returns the handle.

EncodingLimits fields are buffer_bytes, max_depth, max_item_bytes, max_total_bytes: Int?, max_expansion_depth, max_expansion_bytes. safe() is 65536, 256, 16777216, None, 32, 8388608. Valid ranges are buffer_bytes 4096..16777216, max_depth 1..4096, max_item_bytes 1..1073741824, max_total_bytes None or 0..Int.max, max_expansion_depth 0..256, max_expansion_bytes 0..1073741824. Constructors reject the first invalid field before IO with kind Limit, byte_offset 0, empty path, and reason naming field/value/range. Expansion limits apply to XML entities; other codecs retain but do not consume those budgets so one limits type stays stable. max_total_bytes counts wire bytes; max_item_bytes counts decoded bytes retained for one scalar/record/key/object-sort buffer. At every allocator observation, codec-owned live heap is at most buffer_bytes + max_item_bytes + max_expansion_bytes + (256 * max_depth) + 65536 bytes. Codec-owned includes parser/writer state, wire buffers, the current partially decoded item, canonical object-sort storage, and entity-expansion storage; it excludes consumed File-handle storage and values already returned to caller ownership. Counting-allocator tests cover adversarial nesting/items/entities and every legal limit endpoint.

EncodingError fields are format: EncodingFormat, kind: EncodingErrorKind, byte_offset: Int, line: Int?, column: Int?, path: String, reason: String, cause: EncodingCause?. EncodingCause is a Clone+Eq snapshot { kind: String, os_code: Int?, message: String }; it is not IOError and carries no host handle. EncodingError and EncodingCause derive Clone and Eq. cause is Val only for kind IO, otherwise None; cause() returns that snapshot. Display is exactly `<Format> <Kind> at byte <offset>[, line <line>, column <column>][, path <path>]: <reason>` with absent clauses omitted; cause text stays separate. byte_offset is zero-based wire bytes; textual line/column are one-based; path is the best known Data path or empty. The first terminal error is stored; every later method returns an equal clone. Clean EOF is stable None only after full structural validation and trailing-input checks. Runtime parse failures are returned Core values, not new compiler diagnostics; wrong methods/types reuse existing Core type diagnostics. Any new compiler diagnostic still needs diagnostics.md + UI snapshot under I4.

Synchronous blocking is the v1 backpressure law. next reads only until one item or terminal state. write returns only after the item is accepted inside the bound, flushing underlying bytes when needed; no thread, task, channel, callback, hidden queue, WouldBlock, or partial-success status exists. flush pushes bytes but does not validate closure. finish validates closure, flushes, is required for successful output, and is idempotent after success. write after finish returns kind State. Drop closes handles; dropping unfinished output never claims success.

A applicability: JSONReader.next -> DataEvent? ? EncodingError and JSONWriter.write(DataEvent); exactly one root. CBOR uses the same DataEvent and rejects tags, non-text map keys, bignums, or other values outside DataTree as Unsupported, never coercing. DataEvent is Null, Bool(Bool), Int(Int), Float(Float), Text(String), Bytes([U8]), ArrayStart, ArrayEnd, ObjectStart, Key(String), ObjectEnd. JSONWriter rejects DataEvent.Bytes with kind Unsupported and reason `JSON cannot encode Bytes; encode bytes as Text explicitly`, and rejects a Float whose value is NaN or positive/negative infinity with kind Unsupported and reason `JSON cannot encode a non-finite Float`. Validation happens before accepting or emitting bytes for that event; bytes from earlier accepted events may already be flushed. canonical false and true use this identical rejection law. JSON canonical writing buffers/sorts each object within max_item_bytes. JSONLReader.next -> Data?; writer.write(Data); one complete value per non-empty record. CSVReader.next -> [String]?; writer.write([String]); one RFC-4180 record including quoted newlines.

XML is unavailable under this decision alone. XMLReader/XMLWriter may ship only after D-ENCXML1 ratifies the exact event/node algebra, item type, lexical-preservation rule, namespace-expanded names, parse-options type, and field-by-field XML-error-to-EncodingError projection, and this ballot is reconciled to that result. D-ENCXML1's winning schema becomes Option A's conditional XML item schema; this ballot invents no XML type name, variant, payload, or error type. Its winning safe parse options never open external identifiers, preserve or reject general entity references per D-ENCXML1, expand only an explicit in-memory map, reject undeclared references, and charge expansion depth/bytes above. Chunk boundaries cannot change events/errors. Collecting events reconstructs a structurally equal Data/DataTree value to whole parse within limits; Data does not thereby retain source bytes. XML lexical evidence, if later ratified, belongs only to D-ENCXML1 fields, and unchanged-event writing follows that decision's identity law. This ballot cannot ship XML ahead of that representation gate.

Compatibility/evolution: all stream names are new; json.events remains unchanged as specified above. Stream types are non-Codable state handles and cannot be copied. EncodingFormat is exhaustive in v1, so adding a format variant is source-breaking for exhaustive matches and requires an edition-migration decision plus generated rewrite; adding format-specific handles alone does not change the enum. DataEvent changes only if DataTree changes through an owner decision. Beginner pass: whole-value calls remain smallest; JSONL/CSV use an explicit four-line fallible pull loop. Expert pass: ownership, exact event types, byte offsets, namespace/entity law, limits, flush/finish, deterministic output, and backpressure are explicit. Hybrid pass: whole and stream paths use one parser, one DataTree, one error law, and one event algebra.
decisions.story: Mara imports a 40 GB vendor feed, validates each record, and writes a canonical audit stream. New teammates need a small pull loop with ordinary error propagation; operators need fixed memory limits, exact error locations, synchronous backpressure, and explicit completion; library authors need XML and tree-shaped formats to preserve their real structure instead of pretending every format is a line list.

options.name: Codec-native pull handles
options.detail: Each codec exports its own reader/writer type but shares the exact lifecycle, limits, ownership, and error law above. Item types stay truthful: DataEvent for JSON/CBOR, Data for JSONL, rows for CSV, and, conditionally, the exact item schema selected by D-ENCXML1 for XML. Recommended: simple fallible pull control without flattening formats.

options.name: One universal event stream
options.detail: Every existing codec module exports reader and writer, honoring D-ENCSTREAM1, but all return the shared EncodingReader/EncodingWriter. EncodingEvent combines every DataEvent plus Record(Data) and CSVRow([String]). XML contributes no cases until D-ENCXML1 ratifies its exact schema; if reconciled and shipped, EncodingEvent conditionally includes exactly that decision's cases and payloads, with no variants invented here. Constructors remain fallible and consume handles; next/write/flush/finish and terminal errors match common law. Format-invalid variants fail before output. Generic functions can accept one handle type, but every JSON consumer must still account for impossible CSV/XML variants.

options.name: Callback push streams
options.detail: No public handles. Each module exports `read_each(input: ^files.FileReader, visit: fn(Item) -> Bool ? encoding.EncodingError, limits: encoding.EncodingLimits = encoding.EncodingLimits.safe()) -> Void ? encoding.EncodingError`; callback error propagates, while false cancels cleanly after the current item. Each exports `write_each(output: ^files.FileWriter, next: fn() -> Item? ? encoding.EncodingError, limits: encoding.EncodingLimits = encoding.EncodingLimits.safe()) -> Void ? encoding.EncodingError`; json adds `canonical: Bool = false`. write_each pulls until None, propagates producer/codec/IO error, validates closure, flushes, and finishes before success. Item mapping, limits, errors, ownership, and bounded synchronous backpressure match A. XML adds only the parse-options field and item schema later selected by D-ENCXML1. This prevents resuming or composing parser state with ordinary control flow.

comparisons.note: Pull values from an owned reader; serializer owns writer. A adds one bounded error/lifecycle law.
Decoder/Encoder are direct blocking handles. A adds explicit finish and hard memory limits.
Delegate callbacks preserve XML order but invert control. A exposes the same fidelity through fallible pull.

decisions.title: Lossless XML representation over DataTree
decisions.gist: Choose the one lossless XML shape carried by DataTree.
decisions.explainer:
D-ENCSTREAM1=A already requires one core.encoding.xml adapter, one Data/DataTree model, and whole-value plus stream modes. Every option here obeys that ratified boundary; none introduces a second XmlDocument model. This ballot chooses the DataTree node algebra and fidelity level.

Common parser/security law: XML 1.0 Fifth Edition plus Namespaces in XML 1.0 is the v1 floor. parse(String) accepts Unicode text whose declaration is absent or names UTF-8; its identity guarantee is String equality, not original file bytes. parse_bytes([U8]) recognizes UTF-8, UTF-8 BOM, UTF-16LE BOM, and UTF-16BE BOM, validates any XML declaration against detected encoding, and rejects every other encoding with XMLError. to_bytes preserves the original byte sequence when every token is unchanged and the requested output encoding/BOM equals the detected input encoding/BOM. When that encoding/BOM still matches but some tokens change, each unchanged valid raw-byte token is reused independently and each changed/constructed token is rendered in that same encoding; no subtree or whole document is buffered. When output encoding/BOM differs, no raw byte token is reused and every token is transcoded consistently to the requested encoding. Mixed-encoding concatenation is forbidden. No parser opens files, URLs, sockets, catalogs, external subsets, or system/public identifiers.

Predefined and numeric references validate and decode. Declared general references default to Preserve. Reject refuses them. Resolve(values: [String: String]) expands only names present in the explicit in-memory map as character data. Replacement strings are never reparsed as XML markup: `<`, `>`, `&`, quotes, and entity-looking text remain characters and render escaped. Internal declaration replacement text remains inert preservation data. Parameter entities, external parsed entities, and replacement-text markup expansion are Unsupported in v1, not silently normalized; cycles and limits still reject. External identifiers remain inert data. xml.XMLParseOptions owns entity policy and xml.XMLLimits pins max_depth, max_nodes, max_attributes_per_element, max_name_bytes, max_text_bytes, max_entity_declarations, max_entity_depth, and max_entity_replacement_bytes; safe() supplies versioned defaults. Exceeding any limit is an error, never truncation.

Names use XMLName.{ raw, prefix, local, namespace_uri }. Namespace declarations are ordered XMLNamespace.{ prefix, namespace_uri, quote, lexical }. Default namespaces apply to elements, never unprefixed attributes. xml/xmlns bindings and duplicate expanded attributes are validated. Clark keys are local for no namespace and {namespace_uri}local otherwise. Codable projection uses child Clark keys and attribute keys prefixed @. An element is simple-content exactly when every child is text, CDATA, or a resolved entity_ref; their decoded character values concatenate into `$text` (empty children produce `$text: ""`) and `$content` is absent. Otherwise it is mixed-content: `$text` is absent and `$content` is exactly a Data.Array containing every tagged child node in encounter order, including text-like nodes. Repeated child Clark keys become arrays in encounter order only in ordinary child-key projection; `$content` is never regrouped. XML names cannot begin @, $, or {, so control keys do not collide. Existing @[Rename("key")] and @[DenyUnknownFields] apply.

XMLError is exactly XMLError.{ kind: XMLReason, byte_offset: Int?, line: Int?, column: Int?, path: String, reason: String }. XMLReason is the closed enum InvalidEncoding, Malformed, MismatchedTag, InvalidName, Namespace, DuplicateAttribute, Entity, EntityCycle, Limit, Canonicalization, Shape, Unsupported. For source-backed errors byte_offset is Val(zero-based original bytes for parse_bytes or UTF-8 bytes for parse), and line/column are Val(one-based Unicode-scalar positions). Constructed/source-less validation, shape, rendering, and canonicalization errors use None for all three locations, never a colliding numeric sentinel. path remains the best-known Clark-name/index path. parse, parse_bytes, parse_with, canonical, decode, and stream folding return Result; they do not emit diagnostics or partial trees. Diagnostic codes and CLI rendering are downstream gates.

Raw invalidation law for lossless options: lexical evidence is token-local, never a buffered subtree. XMLLexical is the ordinary Data Object {raw_text: Text|Null, raw_bytes: Array<Int>|Null, semantic: Data}; every raw_bytes Int is validated in 0..255; exactly one raw field is non-Null for parsed input and both are Null for constructed tokens. Its semantic snapshot is the lexical-free semantic value of that one token. Element nodes carry open_lexical and close_lexical separately; empty-element syntax has open_lexical and close_lexical Null. Document-whitespace, Text, CDATA, comment, PI, declaration, doctype, entity-ref, attribute, and namespace nodes each carry only their own token lexical. A token slice is valid only when its current lexical-free token value deeply equals semantic. Editing a token invalidates only that token; parent elements have no subtree raw slice. to_string may concatenate valid raw_text tokens with recursively rendered Unicode children. to_bytes may reuse each valid raw_bytes token independently whenever selected output encoding/BOM matches the source; an invalid/changed token is rendered in that same encoding while neighboring valid tokens remain reusable. If selected encoding/BOM differs, all tokens render/transcode and none reuse raw bytes. A streaming element_start can therefore emit complete opening-tag evidence immediately and element_end complete closing-tag evidence without subtree buffering. False snapshots/raw slices are ignored, never trusted; untouched parse-render identity remains exact.

Canonicalization law: xml.XMLCanonical configures `xml.canonical`; canonical processes the resolved semantic infoset, never lexical slices. Inclusive11 means W3C Canonical XML 1.1; Exclusive10 means W3C Exclusive XML Canonicalization 1.0. comments selects the standards' with/without-comments form; inclusive_prefixes is legal only for Exclusive10. V1 canonicalizes the whole document, not arbitrary node sets or XML Signature transforms. Output is UTF-8, LF, no BOM, XML declaration, or DOCTYPE; empty elements expand; entity/character references become characters; namespace declarations and attributes sort exactly per the selected W3C algorithm; escaping and whitespace normalization follow that algorithm. An unresolved entity, relative namespace URI forbidden by the selected standard, or non-document root returns XMLError.

Stream coordination: reader events are document_start, declaration, document_whitespace, doctype, element_start, text, cdata, entity_ref, comment, processing_instruction, element_end, document_end. element_start carries name, ordered namespaces, ordered attributes, empty_style, and opening-token lexical only; element_end carries name and closing-token lexical only. Document-whitespace and leaf events carry only their token-local fields/evidence. Events preserve order and never require subtree buffering. Folding a complete event stream must yield the exact whole-tree semantic DataTree; unfolding that tree must yield the same semantic events. Raw chunks carry the same XMLLexical evidence and limits; no separate stream representation is allowed.

Beginner pass: xml.parse, xml.to_string, xml.decode<T>, safe limits, preserved entities, and ordinary local names need no namespace or DTD ceremony. Expert pass: expanded names, exact byte encoding, lexical evidence, explicit entity resolution, limits, events, C14N mode, comments, and inclusive prefixes are controllable and auditable. Hybrid pass: helpers and Codable are views over the same tagged DataTree/events, not another tree.

Compatibility: current {name, attrs, children, text} output is unratified and lossy. Existing parse/to_string call spelling stays; manual field access migrates to the chosen tags/helpers. The encoding_breadth call site stays, while expected shape and hostile XML corpus are re-pinned. No compatibility alias retains the lossy shape. No compiler dependency/external crate is added.

Downstream gates: exact helper list/signatures beyond those shown; XML stream Reader/Writer ownership and backpressure; diagnostic codes/copy/snapshots; XML conformance corpus/version; canonicalization test-vector provenance; migration tooling for manually inspected old trees. These do not alter the node algebra selected here.

Queued stream error projection is exact. XML reader/writer IO bypasses XMLReason and produces EncodingErrorKind.IO with a populated handle-free EncodingCause; every XMLReason projection has cause=None. InvalidEncoding maps to Syntax. Malformed maps to Truncated only when caused by clean underlying EOF before required XML closure, otherwise Syntax. MismatchedTag, InvalidName, Namespace, DuplicateAttribute, Entity, and Shape map to Syntax. EntityCycle and Limit map to Limit. Canonicalization and Unsupported map to Unsupported. format is XML; path and reason copy unchanged. A present XMLError byte_offset copies unchanged; absent byte_offset maps to the queued EncodingError-required 0 while line/column remain None. Present line/column copy unchanged. This target-only zero is not an XML source-location sentinel: absence is retained by both optional line/column fields and the source-less operation context. No other field is synthesized, and terminal clone/equality follows D-ENCSTREAM-SURFACE1.

`xml.XMLReader.next(&self) -> encoding.Data? ? encoding.EncodingError` returns those events in source order. `xml.XMLWriter.write(&self, item: encoding.Data) -> Void ? encoding.EncodingError` validates one exact event before accepting it, enforces document/declaration/doctype/element state, and emits no bytes for a rejected item; flush/finish follow D-ENCSTREAM-SURFACE1. Folding starts at document_start, converts declaration/doctype and leaf events to their `$xml` node forms, nests element_start through matching element_end (or closes an empty event immediately), and finishes only at document_end, yielding exactly the whole-value document Data.Object. Unfolding performs the inverse key-for-key projection. For every valid whole tree, fold(unfold(tree)) is deep-equal including order and lexical evidence; for every valid complete event sequence, unfold(fold(events)) is event-for-event deep-equal. Invalid order, duplicate document events, post-end input, mismatched end names, or incomplete finish returns State for writer state misuse and Syntax/Truncated for reader wire failures under the queued projection law.

Authoritative whole-node ordinary-Data algebra for A. Public XML values use only encoding.Data Null, Bool, Int, Text, Array, and Object. Byte sequences are Data.Array<Int> with every Int in 0..255. Every object below has exactly the listed keys; every listed key is required even when its value is Null; unknown or missing keys reject. XMLName is exactly {raw:Text,prefix:Text|Null,local:Text,namespace_uri:Text|Null}. XMLLexical is exactly {raw_text:Text|Null,raw_bytes:Data.Array<Int>|Null,semantic:Data}. `$xml` is Text and its closed values are `document`, `document_whitespace`, `declaration`, `doctype`, `element`, `namespace`, `attribute`, `text`, `cdata`, `entity_ref`, `comment`, and `processing_instruction`.

The full node schemas are: document {$xml:"document",encoding:Text|Null,bom:Data.Array<Int>,children:Data.Array<Data>}; document_whitespace {$xml:"document_whitespace",value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; declaration {$xml:"declaration",version:Text,encoding:Text|Null,standalone:Bool|Null,lexical:XMLLexical}; doctype {$xml:"doctype",name:Text,public_id:Text|Null,system_id:Text|Null,internal_subset:Text|Null,lexical:XMLLexical}; element {$xml:"element",name:XMLName,namespaces:Data.Array<Data>,attributes:Data.Array<Data>,children:Data.Array<Data>,empty_style:Text,open_lexical:XMLLexical,close_lexical:XMLLexical|Null}; namespace {$xml:"namespace",prefix:Text|Null,namespace_uri:Text,quote:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; attribute {$xml:"attribute",name:XMLName,parts:Data.Array<Data>,normalized_value:Text|Null,quote:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; text {$xml:"text",value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; cdata {$xml:"cdata",value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; entity_ref {$xml:"entity_ref",name:Text,resolved_value:Text|Null,lexical:XMLLexical}; comment {$xml:"comment",value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; processing_instruction {$xml:"processing_instruction",target:Text,value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}.

Closed payload laws: document children preserve every token in order and may contain document_whitespace/comment/processing_instruction before or after the root, at most one declaration before every other child except leading document_whitespace is forbidden before a declaration, at most one doctype after declaration and before the root, and exactly one root element; no other node tag is legal there. document_whitespace is legal only as a document child outside the root and value contains one or more XML S scalars exactly from U+0020, U+0009, U+000D, U+000A; it preserves prolog spacing, epilog spacing, and trailing newlines. Element namespaces contains only namespace nodes, attributes only attribute nodes, and children only element/text/cdata/entity_ref/comment/processing_instruction nodes. `empty_style` is exactly `"empty"` or `"explicit"`; empty requires children=[], close_lexical=Null, and one empty-element opening token, while explicit requires non-Null close_lexical. `quote` is exactly `"single"` or `"double"`. Attribute parts contains only text or entity_ref nodes. normalized_value is Null exactly when any entity_ref part is unresolved; otherwise it equals the concatenation of text values and resolved entity values after XML 1.0 attribute whitespace normalization. Namespace prefix Null is the default declaration. XML name, namespace, document-order, comment, CDATA, PI, doctype, entity, encoding/BOM, and limit validation follows the earlier standards law and rejects rather than repairing.

Canonical lexical snapshot law: for a parsed token exactly one of raw_text/raw_bytes is non-Null; for a constructed token both are Null. raw_bytes members are Int 0..255. `semantic` is deep-equal to the exact lexical-free semantic payload for that token: declaration/doctype/namespace/attribute/document_whitespace/leaf use their object with lexical removed; element open uses {name,namespaces,attributes,empty_style}; element close uses {name}; document-start uses {encoding,bom}. Nested lexical fields are recursively removed from semantic before comparison. A malformed lexical object, both raw forms present, out-of-range byte, wrong semantic key/type, or unequal snapshot is never trusted: validation treats its raw forms as absent and deterministic rendering proceeds from semantic node fields. Canonicalization always ignores raw forms. No stale raw value can override a changed semantic field.

Authoritative public stream algebra. The item type is exactly encoding.Data; no XMLEvent type or new Data variant exists. Every event is a Data.Object with exactly the listed required keys and no extras. `$xml_event` is Text with the closed values below. document_start {$xml_event:"document_start",encoding:Text|Null,bom:Data.Array<Int>}; document_whitespace {$xml_event:"document_whitespace",value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; declaration {$xml_event:"declaration",version:Text,encoding:Text|Null,standalone:Bool|Null,lexical:XMLLexical}; doctype {$xml_event:"doctype",name:Text,public_id:Text|Null,system_id:Text|Null,internal_subset:Text|Null,lexical:XMLLexical}; element_start {$xml_event:"element_start",name:XMLName,namespaces:Data.Array<Data>,attributes:Data.Array<Data>,empty_style:Text,open_lexical:XMLLexical}; text {$xml_event:"text",value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; cdata {$xml_event:"cdata",value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; entity_ref {$xml_event:"entity_ref",name:Text,resolved_value:Text|Null,lexical:XMLLexical}; comment {$xml_event:"comment",value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; processing_instruction {$xml_event:"processing_instruction",target:Text,value:Text,lexical:XMLLexical}; element_end {$xml_event:"element_end",name:XMLName,close_lexical:XMLLexical}; document_end {$xml_event:"document_end"}. Event namespace/attribute arrays and enum values obey the same closed node laws. An empty element emits element_start with empty_style="empty" and no element_end; explicit emits a matching element_end.

xml.XMLReader.next(&self)->encoding.Data? ? encoding.EncodingError returns that closed event algebra in wire order. xml.XMLWriter.write(&self,item:encoding.Data)->Void ? encoding.EncodingError validates the entire object before accepting it or emitting bytes. Writer state accepts exactly: one document_start; optional declaration; optional doctype; one root element with a LIFO stack of expanded XMLName; XML-legal document_whitespace/comments/PIs; matching explicit element_end; one document_end only after the stack closes; then no further item. It rejects wrong key/type/tag, illegal child class, duplicate/out-of-order declaration/doctype/root/end, empty-style end, mismatched expanded name, post-end item, or finish before document_end. Object-shape/content errors are Syntax; call-order after terminal/finish is State. Folding replaces `$xml_event` with the corresponding `$xml`, nests start/end content, and forms the exact document schema. Unfolding is the inverse. For every valid tree fold(unfold(tree)) is deep-equal including order/lexical evidence; for every valid complete sequence unfold(fold(events)) is event-for-event deep-equal.

Exact xml.XMLLimits law. XMLLimits is exactly {max_depth:Int,max_nodes:Int,max_attributes_per_element:Int,max_name_bytes:Int,max_text_bytes:Int,max_entity_declarations:Int,max_entity_depth:Int,max_entity_replacement_bytes:Int}. safe() is {max_depth:256,max_nodes:1000000,max_attributes_per_element:1024,max_name_bytes:4096,max_text_bytes:16777216,max_entity_declarations:1024,max_entity_depth:32,max_entity_replacement_bytes:8388608}. Inclusive legal ranges are respectively 1..4096, 1..1000000000, 0..1000000, 1..1048576, 0..1073741824, 0..1000000, 0..256, and 0..1073741824. Cross-field requirements are max_entity_depth<=max_depth and max_entity_replacement_bytes<=max_text_bytes. Validation follows declaration order and returns the first bad field/cross-field pair before IO. All byte counts are decoded UTF-8 byte lengths except raw input offsets; node/attribute/entity counts are exact nonnegative integers. Counters and prospective additions use arbitrary-precision nonnegative arithmetic before comparison, so host integer overflow cannot wrap, pass, allocate, or truncate; a bound crossing returns Limit before retaining the crossing item.

Conditional stream constructors under D-ENCSTREAM-SURFACE1=A are `xml.reader(input:^files.FileReader, limits:encoding.EncodingLimits=encoding.EncodingLimits.safe(), xml:xml.XMLParseOptions=xml.XMLParseOptions.safe())->xml.XMLReader ? encoding.EncodingError` and `xml.writer(output:^files.FileWriter, limits:encoding.EncodingLimits=encoding.EncodingLimits.safe(), xml:xml.XMLRenderOptions=xml.XMLRenderOptions.safe())->xml.XMLWriter ? encoding.EncodingError`. `xml.XMLParseOptions` is exactly {entities:xml.XMLEntityPolicy=.Preserve, limits:xml.XMLLimits=xml.XMLLimits.safe()}; XMLEntityPolicy is `.Preserve`, `.Reject`, or `.Resolve([String:String])`. `xml.XMLRenderOptions` is exactly {encoding:xml.XMLEncoding=.UTF8, lexical:xml.XMLLexicalPolicy=.PreserveValid}; XMLEncoding is `.UTF8`, `.UTF8BOM`, `.UTF16LE`, or `.UTF16BE`, and XMLLexicalPolicy is `.PreserveValid` or `.Deterministic`. Canonicalization remains the separate `xml.canonical(..., xml.XMLCanonical)` operation and is not a writer option. Constructor validation is deterministic before IO: validate shared EncodingLimits in its declared field order, then XMLLimits in max_depth, max_nodes, max_attributes_per_element, max_name_bytes, max_text_bytes, max_entity_declarations, max_entity_depth, max_entity_replacement_bytes order, then entity-map keys/values or render enums. The first failure wins and projects through EncodingError.

Both limit objects remain active; neither silently overrides the other. The effective depth ceiling is min(encoding.max_depth, xml.max_depth). Wire buffering and total input use encoding.buffer_bytes/max_total_bytes. One retained event/tree item and canonical-sort storage use encoding.max_item_bytes. Element/node/name/text/attribute/declaration counts use their xml.XMLLimits fields. Entity expansion uses min(encoding.max_expansion_depth, xml.max_entity_depth) and min(encoding.max_expansion_bytes, xml.max_entity_replacement_bytes), while max_entity_declarations remains XML-only. Crossing either contributing bound reports Limit naming the actual bound first crossed. The allocator ceiling remains the queued shared encoding limit law; XML limits may reduce work but never enlarge it. Whole-value parse_with applies XMLLimits alone because it has no stream EncodingLimits; stream reader always applies both as above.

Document-whitespace fold/render law. Reader emits one document_whitespace event for each maximal contiguous XML S token outside the root, without coalescing across a comment, PI, declaration, doctype, or root boundary. Fold maps it key-for-key to the document_whitespace node; unfold maps each node back one-for-one, so prolog spaces, epilog spaces, CR/LF spelling, and a final newline survive. Writer rejects it inside an element, before a declaration, or after document_end. to_string/to_bytes render its value exactly when lexical evidence is valid, otherwise render the validated XML S value; canonicalization discards document_whitespace outside the document element as required by the selected C14N standard.

Bounded byte-reuse and declaration law. parse_bytes records one document source_encoding and source_bom in document encoding/bom. The renderer decides reuse from those two bounded facts plus each token snapshot; it never scans or buffers the whole document to choose. Reuse is permitted only when xml.XMLRenderOptions encoding/BOM exactly equals source_encoding/source_bom. Under that condition a valid unchanged token writes its raw_bytes directly and a changed/constructed token writes deterministic bytes in the same selected encoding; memory remains the active stream buffer plus one token/item. If encoding/BOM differs, every token is transcoded and raw_bytes are ignored. An XML declaration with encoding Null is legal for every supported BOM/encoding and renders with the encoding pseudo-attribute absent. A non-Null declaration encoding must case-insensitively name the selected family (UTF-8 versus UTF-16); deterministic rendering uses canonical `UTF-8` or `UTF-16`, and conflict returns InvalidEncoding before any bytes, including when raw evidence exists. Untouched parse_bytes plus matching render options reuses every token, including document_whitespace, and is byte-for-byte identical; token-local edits preserve unchanged-token bytes without whole-document buffering.

Exact XMLLimits counter membership and scope. `max_nodes` counts every accepted `$xml` object in the folded whole tree, including document, declaration, document_whitespace, doctype, each element, namespace, attribute, text, cdata, entity_ref, comment, and processing_instruction. XMLName and XMLLexical helper Objects are not additional nodes. In streaming, document_start accounts for the document node; declaration/document_whitespace/doctype/element_start/leaf events account for their corresponding node plus every namespace/attribute carried by element_start; element_end and document_end add zero. The prospective increment is checked before retaining/emitting the event.

`max_depth` counts element nesting only: document is depth 0, the root element is depth 1, each child element is parent depth+1, and non-element nodes do not change depth. `max_attributes_per_element` counts attribute nodes only and excludes namespace declarations. `max_name_bytes` applies separately to the UTF-8 byte length of every non-Null XMLName raw, prefix, local, and namespace_uri field; declaration version/encoding, doctype name/public_id/system_id, namespace prefix/URI, entity name, and PI target are each also checked separately against it. No concatenated or normalized form may bypass its own component check.

`max_text_bytes` is both a per-field and whole-document ceiling. It counts UTF-8 bytes of document_whitespace value; text/cdata/comment value; PI value; doctype internal_subset; attribute text-part values and resolved entity values; and every other free-text payload not governed by max_name_bytes. normalized_value, lexical raw/snapshot fields, and the same resolved value appearing again in normalized_value are not double-counted. Each counted field must be <= max_text_bytes and the arbitrary-precision cumulative sum across the document must also be <= it.

`max_entity_declarations` counts general plus parameter declarations encountered in the internal subset, even when unsupported policy later rejects use. `max_entity_depth` counts the root replacement as depth 1 and each recursively referenced replacement as parent+1; preserved/unresolved references consume depth 0. `max_entity_replacement_bytes` is both per replacement and cumulative: each decoded replacement UTF-8 length and the arbitrary-precision sum of all replacement bytes materialized during one parse must be <= it. Repeated expansion is charged every time materialized; rejected/preserved inert text is not charged. Every counter uses prospective arbitrary-precision addition and returns Limit before allocation/retention on crossing.

Stream-decision dependency is explicit. The public encoding.Data event ABI, XMLReader/XMLWriter methods, shared encoding.EncodingLimits precedence, queued EncodingError projection, and the constructor signatures in this ballot become operative only if D-ENCSTREAM-SURFACE1 ratifies A. If it ratifies B or C, XML whole-node semantics remain decided here, but every public XML stream type, callback/handle signature, event wrapper, error projection, and dual-limit entrypoint must be reconciled to that winning option in a follow-up ballot before implementation; none of this ballot's A-conditional stream spellings may ship by assumption.
decisions.story: Mina receives signed healthcare XML containing namespaces, mixed text, comments, processing instructions, CDATA, and entity references. She must decode ordinary records with @[Codable], inspect every node, verify a standards-defined canonical signature form, and write untouched input back exactly. Today's delimiter scanner trims and reorders text, skips comments and processing instructions, has no CDATA/DTD/entity model, and keeps prefixes without resolving namespace identities, so a successful parse can corrupt the document.

options.name: Nested tagged XML nodes in ordinary DataTree
options.detail: Recommended. The document is one tagged ordinary Data.Object containing a nested ordered tree and uses the exact explainer schema. An element has name, ordered namespaces, ordered attributes, children, empty_style, open_lexical, and close_lexical; close_lexical is Null only for empty-element syntax. Declaration, doctype, namespace, attribute, text, cdata, entity_ref, comment, and processing_instruction each carry their own token-local lexical field. XMLName and XMLLexical are exact ordinary Data.Objects; raw bytes and BOM are Array<Int> with every value validated 0..255, never an invented Data Bytes variant. All optional values are Data.Null, required arrays are present, extra keys reject, and recursive validation/rendering follows the exact common law. The nested shape makes parent/child inspection and Codable projection direct while preserving order and token-local evidence without subtree buffering. Its public stream item is the exact tagged encoding.Data event algebra and constructor/dual-limit law in the explainer; no XMLEvent type is introduced. Document-level XML S is an exact document_whitespace node/event, preserving prolog/epilog spacing and trailing newlines under the token-local encoding-compatible reuse law.

options.name: Native XML variants added to Data
options.detail: Explicitly amend ratified D-ENC-DYN1 by adding native Data variants XMLDocument, XMLDeclaration, XMLDoctype, XMLElement, XMLNamespace, XMLAttribute, XMLText, XMLCData, XMLEntityRef, XMLComment, and XMLProcessingInstruction. This option is not compatible with D-ENC-DYN1 as currently ratified; choosing B is the owner decision to reopen its closed ordinary-Data algebra and requires that decision log and every exhaustive consumer to migrate. Payloads otherwise match A exactly: XMLElement carries name, ordered namespaces/attributes/children, empty_style, open_lexical, and nullable close_lexical; all other variants carry the same token-local lexical fields, XMLName shape, validated 0..255 byte arrays, validation, rendering, stream, and error laws. Invalid tagged shapes become unrepresentable, but every JSON/YAML/TOML/CBOR/Codable walker, comptime/JIT value, formatter, accessor, and exhaustive Data match must define the new variants.

options.name: Normalized infoset nodes in DataTree
options.detail: Use A's nested tags, expanded names, attributes, mixed-order children, comments, and processing instructions, but omit XMLLexical. CDATA becomes text; entity and character spelling becomes characters after bounded resolution; declaration/DOCTYPE lexical detail and original encoding disappear. to_string emits one deterministic UTF-8 spelling. This is semantically faithful for most data exchange and fully compatible with one DataTree/stream model, but parse-render identity, source-preserving edits, and byte-signature workflows are explicitly unsupported.

options.name: Tagged event tape as the whole DataTree
options.detail: Represent the whole document as Data.Array of tagged stream events rather than a nested element tree. element_start carries expanded name, namespaces, ordered attributes, empty_style, and open_lexical; element_end carries name and close_lexical; leaf events match the common stream schema. parse returns this tape and streaming yields it incrementally; xml.root/content helpers build indexed views over the tape without storing another tree. Roundtrip and C14N remain possible, and D-ENCSTREAM1's one DataTree is honored. Parent/child navigation, Codable projection, subtree edits, and structural validation require stack/index reconstruction on every consumer.

comparisons.note: quick-xml exposes ordered Start/Text/CData/Comment/Decl/PI/DocType events. D is closest; A folds the same honest event vocabulary into a navigable DataTree.
comparisons.code: match reader.read_event_into(&mut buf)? { Event::Start(e) => handle(e), Event::CData(c) => handle(c), Event::Comment(c) => handle(c), _ => {} }

comparisons.note: lxml has expanded Clark names, entity controls, comments/PIs, and C14N over a dedicated tree. A keeps those capabilities inside Jet's already-ratified shared DataTree.
comparisons.code:
parser = XMLParser(resolve_entities=False, no_network=True)
root = fromstring(raw, parser)
write_c14n(root, exclusive=True, with_comments=False)

comparisons.note: Go token order and expanded names are strong, but Marshal/Unmarshal is not lexical round-trip storage. A combines token-order truth with explicit validated lexical evidence.
comparisons.code: for { tok, err := dec.Token(); if err != nil { break }; switch tok.(type) { case xml.StartElement, xml.CharData, xml.ProcInst: } }

comparisons.note: DOM distinguishes text, CDATA, comment, PI, and document-type nodes; C14N defines signature bytes independently of source spelling. A uses that separation: semantic nodes for C14N, lexical evidence for exact preservation.
comparisons.code:
Document -> Element -> [Text, CDATASection, Comment, ProcessingInstruction]
