decisions.title: VS Code and Zed debugger discovery and launch experience
decisions.gist: Choose how Jet debugging appears and starts in VS Code and Zed.
decisions.explainer:
Scope and inherited law. Ratified D-DBG1 makes `jet debug <file>` the only public debugger command. D-DBG2 keeps generated/backend frames hidden unless raw frames are explicitly enabled. D-DBG3 fixes debugger command meaning. D-OBS2 owns `.jetmap`. Live open D-DBG-DAP1 owns wire behavior and capabilities; D-DBG-AUTH1 is live, open, and unratified; it owns the proposed consent, path, environment, secret, attach-proof, and workspace-authority law but grants nothing until the owner chooses an outcome. D-DBG-DIAG1 is absent from Tower; its /tmp artifact is a draft only. EDITOR1 cannot ship authority- or diagnostic-dependent integration until AUTH1 and DIAG1 are both ratified compatibly. AUTH1 would own consent, paths, environment, secrets, attach proof, and workspace authority; live open, unratified D-DBG-NATIVE1 owns native backend support, discovery, identity, and diagnostics. EDITOR1 chooses editor discovery and launch UX only. It cannot widen any other outcome. Native launch/attach UI remains dormant until DAP1, AUTH1, and NATIVE1 ratify compatible support; interpreter-backed launch can ship independently. If DAP1 or AUTH1 rejects attach, editors do not register, generate, suggest, or accept an attach configuration.

Current clean audit. `editors/vscode/package.json` activates on Jet language and contributes language, grammar, LSP settings, and Run/Test commands only; it has no `contributes.debuggers`, debug configuration provider, adapter descriptor, Debug command, initial configuration, or editor acceptance test. Its executable discovery is explicit `jet.languageServerPath`, then compiler-workspace `target/debug/jet`, then PATH. `editors/zed/extension.toml` and its WASM register Jet language and `jet lsp` only; they have no debug-adapter registration or debug scenarios. Existing VSIX/WASM files are build artifacts, not proof of debugger behavior.

One executable, one adapter. Every enabled editor integration resolves one Jet driver executable and invoke it directly with argv `["debug","--dap",<canonical-program>]`; no terminal text, shell, task wrapper, backend command, or alternate adapter binary. The source program is the CLI argument, matching DAP1; editor launch JSON cannot send a second conflicting program. The adapter receives launch/attach fields through DAP after initialization. The editor never discovers LLDB, CDB, formatters, or toolchains. When a selected program requires native debugging, the launched Jet driver alone applies the ratified NATIVE1 discovery/tool-identity law; until that law is ratified, the editor must not claim native availability or implement its own fallback. Interpreter/native selection remains Jet's existing one-command boundary.

Jet driver discovery is deterministic and shared by LSP, Run, Test, and Debug. VS Code setting `jet.executablePath` and Zed's standard per-language binary override are the only explicit overrides; each must resolve to an absolute regular executable. Otherwise a compiler-development workspace identified by verified Jet repository markers may use its canonical `target/debug/jet`; otherwise resolve `jet` through the editor host's direct executable lookup. No recursive workspace search, downloaded binary, sibling extension, task, shell profile, or debugger-backend PATH search. The extension runs `jet --version --json` once, requires the compatible CLI/editor protocol version, caches identity for that window, and rechecks file identity before each spawn. Missing/incompatible Jet gets one Jet-owned action: install/update Jet or set the executable override. Existing `jet.languageServerPath` is read only as a migration input: if set and `jet.executablePath` is empty, show the resolved value and offer an explicit one-click settings migration; never silently copy or keep two active discovery laws.

Option-scoped VS Code registration. Under A, The extension contributes debugger `type:"jet"`, label `Jet Debugger`, language `jet`, and configuration attributes for request `launch` plus conditional `attach`. It contributes `Jet: Debug Current File`, `Jet: Debug Package Entry`, and—only when attach is ratified—`Jet: Attach to Local Jet Process`. A dynamic DebugConfigurationProvider supplies no-config launch and schema validation; a DebugAdapterDescriptorFactory returns the direct Jet executable/argv above. Initial configurations are named `Jet: Debug current file` and `Jet: Debug package entry`; attach is added only under compatible ratification. F5 with an active runnable Jet file chooses it. Package entry resolution never invents a public command. The extension invokes the private, versioned editor bridge directly. Exact argv is `["__editor","debug-targets","--schema","jet.editor.debug-targets/v1","--anchor",<canonical active file or workspace root>,"--auth-handle",<inherited handle number>]`. This private spelling is ratified only as extension/compiler protocol, omitted from help/completions/manpages, and never executes user code. Before spawn, the installed hash-recorded extension creates a private non-inheritable-by-default local socket pair/Windows anonymous pipe, marks exactly the child endpoint inheritable, generates 32 random bytes from the OS CSPRNG, and writes `{schema:"jet.editor.bridge-auth/v1",nonce:<64 lowercase hex>,editorPid:<decimal>,expiresAt:<monotonic now+10s>}` to that endpoint after spawn. `--auth-handle` names only that inherited endpoint; no nonce appears in argv/env/files. Jet does not trust any extension-asserted hash. The signed Jet release manifest separately pins editor product id, publisher/code-signing identity, extension id+version, distribution archive SHA-256, canonical unpacked-tree SHA-256, required component SHA-256+byte length, and allowed parent-chain shape. VS Code components are at least `package.json`, `extension.js`, grammar/config/schema assets; Zed components are `extension.toml`, `extension.wasm`, language config, grammar, and debug schema when B enables it. Archive hash never stands in for installed bytes. Canonical tree hash is SHA-256 over sorted records for every regular installed file: ASCII `jet.extension-tree/v1\\0`, relative path encoded UTF-8 NFC with `/` separators and u32-LE length, executable bit byte 0/1, file byte length u64 LE, and file SHA-256; reject non-UTF-8 paths, symlinks, duplicate normalized paths, devices, and files absent from the signed manifest. Jet walks the OS process parent chain from direct child to extension host to signed VS Code/Zed executable, checks same user/session and OS code-signing identity where available, then receives no-follow read-only handles for the installed extension manifest and executable JS/WASM over the private channel (SCM_RIGHTS on Unix; DuplicateHandle from the authenticated parent on Windows), hashes bytes and lengths from those handles, enumerates installed files no-follow to recompute the canonical tree hash, and requires archive-recorded manifest identity, every component hash, and installed-tree hash to match the signed release manifest. Linux packages without OS signing must match the release-manifest executable hash. Jet then verifies nonce length/hex, expiry, single read, and EOF and closes every handle before target enumeration. Missing, redirected, replayed, inherited-by-grandchild, wrong-parent, expired, or trailing data rejects E2236. This authenticates the private bridge only; it cannot approve AUTH. Stdout is exactly one UTF-8 JSON object `{"schema":"jet.editor.debug-targets/v1","workspace":<canonical path>,"targets":[{"id":"sha256:<64 lowercase hex>","label":String,"program":<canonical .jet path>,"packageRoot":<canonical path>,"source":"active-file"|"package-entry"}]}`; stderr is empty on success and diagnostics use the shared editor protocol on failure. Target id is SHA-256 over tagged binary bytes, not ambiguous JSON. Input is ASCII `jet.debug-target/v1\0`, then each identity length-prefixed with a little-endian u32: POSIX identity is tag 0x01 + `st_dev` u64 LE + `st_ino` u64 LE; Windows identity is tag 0x02 + volume serial u64 LE + FILE_ID_128's 16 bytes; absent package root is tag 0x00. For a package target append tag 0x03 + SHA-256 of the exact no-follow-opened `pkg.jet` bytes + SHA-256 of canonical selected-entry bytes `{"schema":"jet.package-entry/v1","entry":<workspace-relative UTF-8 NFC path>}` with keys in that order and no whitespace; standalone targets append tag 0x04. Append workspace-relative program path as UTF-8 NFC with `/` separators, length-prefixed u32. Non-UTF-8 paths reject E2236. Any file-id, package manifest byte, canonical entry declaration, package root, or relative path change changes id. Targets are sorted by id. Zero targets produces E2236/no runnable file; one launches; multiple always show a picker. Generated config persists canonical `program`, never id; every launch reopens/canonicalizes program and re-resolves package membership, so stale ids cannot redirect execution. The extension never guesses `main.jet`, parses `pkg.jet`, or scans files. Schema/version mismatch is E2236 and no fallback.

Conditional Zed registration. The released baseline is Zed Rust extension API `zed_extension_api = "0.7.0"`. Its exact contract is `extension.toml` section `[debug_adapters.Jet]` with `schema_path = "debug_adapter_schemas/Jet.json"`, plus Extension methods `get_dap_binary`, `dap_request_kind`, and `dap_config_to_scenario`; A does not register any Zed adapter, locator, schema, or scenario under API 0.7.0 because its trust/auth requirements are not realizable. B may register the stated adapter only if a separately ratified AUTH outcome provides an editor-independent OS broker that authenticates Zed without a trust API; otherwise B also disables Zed. A future Zed-capable outcome may use `dap_locator_create_scenario` only after a pinned released API supplies the missing trust fact. `get_dap_binary` returns command=<resolved Jet executable>, arguments=[`debug`,`--dap`,<canonical program>], empty added env, cwd=<authorized cwd>, stdio connection, and the launch/conditional-attach request args. The extension never downloads Jet. The only Zed adapter override is the standard `dap.Jet.binary`, received as `user_provided_debug_adapter_path`, and it is treated as `jet.executablePath`; `dap.Jet.args` is rejected because adapter argv is fixed.

Exact `.zed/debug.json` is an array. Jet entries accept `{"adapter":"Jet","label":String,"request":"launch","program":String,"args":[String],"cwd":String,"env":{String:String},"stopOnEntry":Bool,"showRawFrames":Bool}`; conditional attach replaces launch fields with positive `processId`, `program`, `map`, and optional `showRawFrames`. Example: `[{"adapter":"Jet","label":"Jet: API","request":"launch","program":"$ZED_WORKTREE_ROOT/src/api.jet","args":["--port","8080"],"cwd":"$ZED_WORKTREE_ROOT","env":{"LOG_LEVEL":"debug"},"stopOnEntry":false,"showRawFrames":false}]`. Unknown fields reject through the shipped schema. Zed's `dap.Jet.binary` overrides only the Jet driver; it never names LLDB/CDB.

Zed 0.7.0 exposes DAP registration but no extension API that proves workspace trusted/restricted state or authenticates a Jet-owned approval window. Therefore, while AUTH1 remains open/unratified, Zed integration is planning only; if the owner ratifies AUTH1 with its current broker law, Zed 0.7.0 cannot satisfy A's automatic locator or AUTH editor-token path: A registers no Zed debug adapter, Debug item, locator, scenario, schema, or debug command until a released Zed API provides both facts. A may expose only non-debug `Jet: Debugger Status` command/language status text explaining the pinned API prerequisite; it cannot start Jet or resemble a launch action. Clean-install acceptance must fail before claiming Zed support if any Debug UI item appears. Explicit `.zed/debug.json` under B is also unsupported if AUTH requires that missing trust signal. C may expose a terminal command only when Zed itself labels it a user-confirmed task; it is never called integrated debugging. A later released API version may replace 0.7.0 only after the ballot contract, version, and acceptance are updated; “current stable” alone is not a version pin.

Option boundaries. A registers contextual/no-config providers, package-target bridge calls, and ordinary Debug-button behavior in VS Code only; Zed is explicitly disabled and excluded from A acceptance until a pinned released trust/auth API exists. B registers the adapter and schema in VS Code and may do so in Zed only if the ratified editor-independent AUTH broker proves signed Zed identity and human approval without extension trust state; otherwise Zed is disabled. B it never calls the target bridge automatically and launches solely from an explicit `launch.json` or `.zed/debug.json`. C registers no debugger, adapter, provider, locator, schema, initial configuration, breakpoint integration, or acceptance claim; its commands are terminal wrappers around public `jet debug <file>` and cannot present editor stacks/variables. Common acceptance language applies only to behavior each option claims.

Configuration law. Editor configuration is a projection onto DAP1/AUTH1, not a second policy. No editor schema contains a separate secret-name field: AUTH classifies every requested `env` name and derives any secret grant inside the authenticated approval broker. Secret classification, secret-name grants, and approval tokens are never transported in DAP JSON, launch files, `.zed/debug.json`, or adapter argv. Launch accepts `type:"jet"`, `request:"launch"`, `name`, `program`, `args:[String]`, `cwd`, `env:{String:String}`, `stopOnEntry:Bool`, and `showRawFrames:Bool`; defaults are active/resolved program, empty args, package/workspace root cwd, empty explicit env, true, and false. Unknown Jet fields fail with the editor's schema error; no shell-string args. `program` must be one canonical local `.jet` file accepted by the Jet driver. Attach, only if ratified, accepts `type`, `request:"attach"`, `name`, positive integer `processId`, canonical `program`, canonical `map`, and `showRawFrames`; process picker results come from a Jet-owned, authority-filtered query and display redacted PID/image/build identity, never arbitrary OS command lines. Editor variables such as workspace folder are expanded by the client once, then Jet canonicalizes and authorizes the result. Any authority-sensitive field change creates a new AUTH preview hash.

Option-scoped beginner law. Only A provides zero-config launch. On trusted VS Code workspaces, gutter breakpoints and the ordinary editor Debug action work without checked-in configuration. The active runnable Jet file wins; package entry is the explicit second action, never a hidden replacement. A generated initial configuration is an editable suggestion, not required state. Defaults expose no raw frames, secret inheritance, external cwd, attach, backend script, or remote authority. The first material launch still displays AUTH1's redacted authority preview and uses its preview-hash-bound approval token; editor workspace trust is not approval. Cancel, EOF, denial, or editor disconnect before token consumption causes zero build/run/attach effects.

Workspace trust. In an untrusted/restricted workspace, every enabled integration provides syntax coloring and read-only language metadata but do not start Jet, LSP, Run, Test, package metadata, debug adapter, process picker, or executable probes against workspace paths. Debug commands explain that editor workspace trust is required. Granting editor trust merely allows Jet to start; it does not grant AUTH1 authority, environment, secrets, scripts, attach, native backend, or remote access. Checked-in launch/scenario configuration is data and receives the same schema, canonicalization, preview, and redaction as interactive launch. Extension logs never contain environment values, secret names when policy redacts them, approval tokens, raw values, backend output, or foreign command lines.

Editor diagnostic contract. E2236 remains a draft DIAG1 allocation, not live law until D-DBG-DIAG1 ratifies; EDITOR cannot emit it early. Exact What is `Jet debug configuration is invalid`. Each failure chooses one byte-pinned Why/Fix pair: Why `field <field> <constraint>`; Fix `correct <field> in the editor's Jet debug configuration`. Why `no runnable Jet file is active`; Fix `open a runnable .jet file or choose Jet: Debug package entry`. Why `package entry selection is ambiguous: <workspace-relative entries>`; Fix `choose one package entry explicitly`. Why `Jet extension protocol <editor-version> is incompatible with Jet <jet-version>`; Fix `update Jet and the Jet editor extension to compatible versions`. Why `the private editor bridge could not authenticate the installed extension`; Fix `reinstall the Jet extension and restart the editor, then retry`. Why `target path cannot be represented by jet.editor.debug-targets/v1`; Fix `move the Jet source to a UTF-8 path, then retry`. Every pair gets diagnostics.md, jet explain, plain/TTY/JSON/DAP/editor snapshots, exact exit, redaction, and hostile field/path fixtures under I4. Until DIAG1 ratifies, the feature is blocked rather than borrowing another code.

Diagnostics and UX truth. Adapter launch failures surface the structured Jet/DAP diagnostic and one relevant action; extensions do not rewrite backend/rustc text or infer success from process creation. Status UI distinguishes interpreter session, native session, unavailable native backend, authority approval needed, and unsupported attach. Capability-driven UI hides unsupported actions; it never advertises a grayed feature as shipped. Restart, disconnect, terminate, breakpoint, variables, evaluate, output, and attach semantics come only from DAP1. All editor strings say Jet, Jet source, and Jet Debugger; generated Rust and DAP jargon stay out of beginner surfaces.

Option-scoped clean-install acceptance. A proves the full zero-config matrix below in VS Code and proves Zed 0.7.0 has no Jet adapter/button/locator and shows one unsupported-version explanation. B proves VS Code adapter/schema/explicit-config launch and no zero-config provider; Zed runs the same explicit-config matrix only when the independent AUTH broker prerequisite is ratified and proved, otherwise B proves Zed disabled. C proves command/task wrappers and asserts no debugger registration, F5 integration, stacks, or variables. Test released, unpacked artifacts—not source-only mocks—on fresh user profiles with no settings, launch files, scenarios, cached server, PATH pollution, or prior Jet extension. Install the pinned supported VS Code release and Zed 0.7.0 host plus a release Jet executable, open (1) one standalone `.jet` file and (2) a package whose path, file, args, and cwd include spaces and non-ASCII. In every client claimed by the selected option prove extension activation and shared executable identity. Only A/VS Code proves ordinary Debug with zero config; B proves explicit configuration only; disabled Zed rows prove no registration or execution. Claimed integrated rows prove: breakpoint binding on exact Jet line; stop/step/continue; Jet stack/locals; ordered stdout/stderr; nonzero exit; cancel before approval causes zero effects; workspace-untrusted suppression; malformed config rejection; missing/incompatible Jet repair; and no generated/backend leakage. Conditional native rows use the exact NATIVE1 clean-host matrix and cannot skip a supported host for a missing backend. Conditional attach rows prove the Jet-owned picker, identity preview, true attach, detach+continue, and mismatch rejection. Capture scrubbed editor/DAP transcripts and UI screenshots; fail on console errors, hidden fallback, shell spawn, stale packaged artifact, or capability mismatch. The VSIX is rebuilt, installed, and hash-recorded. A's disabled Zed row installs the released WASM/manifest, invokes only `Jet: Debugger Status`, and proves it contains no debug registration or Debug item; B hash-records a Zed debugger artifact only when its AUTH prerequisite is met.

Beginner pass: in A's supported VS Code release, install extension, open Jet file, set breakpoint, press Debug; Zed truthfully says integrated Jet debugging is unavailable rather than presenting a broken path. no configuration, adapter choice, backend choice, or package knowledge. Expert pass: file/package selection, argv, cwd, explicit environment names and broker-derived secret classification, raw frames, executable override, exact identity, audit, and conditional verified attach are available through standard editor configuration. Hybrid pass: every enabled editor entrypoint resolves one Jet driver and project the same DAP, AUTH, NATIVE, map, diagnostics, and debugger model; editor convenience never becomes a second execution path.
decisions.story: Maya installs the Jet extension, opens a new `hello.jet`, adds a breakpoint, and presses the editor's ordinary Debug button. She expects Jet to choose that file, stop on Jet source, and show Jet values without first learning DAP or writing configuration. Later, her teammate Arun needs package arguments, a staging cwd, selected environment names, raw frames, and—if attach is ratified—a verified local process attach, all without the editor inventing a second debugger path or silently trusting the workspace.

decisions.detail:
Recommend A. VS Code gets a real zero-config Jet debugger — active-file and package discovery plus expert launch and conditional-attach configuration — while Zed integration is truthfully disabled under API 0.7.0 until a pinned released trust/auth API can satisfy AUTH, rather than shipping a button that looks live but cannot prove workspace trust or approval identity. B requires checked-in configuration in every editor; C never connects editor breakpoints, stacks, or variables at all.

Tier compatibility (D-CANVAS-DEBUG-UX1). EDITOR1 already names the engine: its status UI distinguishes interpreter session, native session, unavailable native backend, authority-approval-needed, and unsupported attach, and interpreter-backed launch ships independently of the native path. That matches the ratified tier-aware direction — one Jet driver resolves and projects the same DAP, AUTH, NATIVE, map, and diagnostic model whether the run is compiled (native session) or under `jet dev` (in-tier session), and editor convenience never becomes a second execution path. The editor-UX axis chosen here — zero-config / explicit-config / commands-only — is independent of which engine tier is running underneath.

comparisons.note: Rust commonly splits language service and debugger ownership across extensions, so users must align tool discovery and launch configuration themselves. A keeps Jet language service and Jet-owned DAP behind one verified Jet executable and one extension.

Go's extension offers zero-config debugging for the active file/package while retaining launch.json controls. A adopts that progressive-disclosure shape but keeps authority preview and backend discovery in the Jet driver.
comparisons.code:
F5 on main.go  -> debug active package
F5 on hello.jet -> debug active Jet file

comparisons.note: Python exposes a first-run debugger choice and rich configurations, but interpreter selection can become editor-specific state. Jet avoids a parallel editor runtime selector: the extension chooses only the Jet driver, and Jet owns interpreter/native selection.

Python: Select Interpreter
Jet: no engine picker; jet debug chooses the ratified engine

decisions.title: Debugger diagnostics, exits, and recovery
decisions.gist: Choose how debugger failures are named, translated, exited, and recovered.
decisions.explainer:
Scope and dependencies. D-DBG1/2/3 and D-OBS2 remain law. Live open D-DBG-DAP1 owns framing, states, lifecycle, and message ids 22031..22038. Live open D-DBG-NATIVE1 owns E2205 missing/incompatible/untrusted tool and E2206 unsupported host. D-DBG-AUTH1 is live, open, and unratified; its proposed authority law grants nothing until the owner selects an outcome. D-DBG-EDITOR1 is live, open, and unratified; its proposed registration/configuration law grants nothing until the owner selects an outcome. If AUTH1 and EDITOR1 are ratified compatibly, AUTH uses E2240 approval, E2241 environment, E2242 path, E2243 attach authority, E2244 backend authority, E2245 remote; EDITOR contributes E2236 variants below. DIAG1 never changes their authority or UI policy.

Canonical terminal frame for every selected option is exactly four LF-terminated UTF-8 lines, with no headline outside What: `Error [<code>] [<class>]\n What: <what>\n Why: <why>\n Fix: <fix>\n`. Class is exactly `user`, `tool`, or `internal`; brackets, capitalization, one leading space on What/Why/Fix, colon placement, and field order are invariant. ANSI may wrap tokens only in TTY mode and stripping ANSI must reproduce these exact bytes. Related diagnostics follow as separate complete frames; no duplicated headline, `Class:` line, or class suffix after the Fix.

Common laws for every option. Every user/tool failure has a stable Jet E-code, What/Why/Fix, class, redaction, I4 snapshots, and exit/lifecycle truth. A CLI parse failure before a debug request exists is exit 2 and uses existing usage diagnostics. A terminal debug request failure after valid CLI parsing is exit 1. A terminal user cancellation before effect is 0; E2204 remains current interpreted early-quit law. A debuggee completion is not an adapter/request failure: terminal returns existing 0 or runtime 70, DAP emits exited with the real debuggee code then terminated, and a clean adapter exits 0. A failed correlated DAP request receives exactly one failure response but does not by itself exit the adapter; state/lifecycle below decides whether it remains usable. Fatal unsynchronized protocol loss exits adapter 1. Internal invariant failure exits terminal/adapter 101 after fail-closed cleanup. No option turns backend/editor prose into source truth or acknowledges failure as success.

Option A only — specific codes and exact copy. E2230 launch: class user for build/drift/process-create variants and tool for first-frame loss. What `debug launch could not start the selected Jet program`. Why exactly one: `the debug build failed with the Jet diagnostic above`; `the verified program disappeared or changed before launch`; `the operating system denied process creation`; `the program stopped before the debugger established its first Jet frame`. Fix respectively: `fix the earlier Jet diagnostic, then run jet debug <file> again`; `run jet debug <file> again to rebuild and revalidate the program`; `allow this user to start the program, then retry`; `run jet debug <file> again; if it repeats, rerun with --audit <filename> and report E2230`.
E2231 tool attach-after-authority: What `debugger could not attach to the authorized process`. Why `the verified process exited before attach completed`, `the operating system revoked process-control permission`, or `the debugger engine rejected the verified target`. Fix `choose the process again; Jet will revalidate identity and ask for new authority`.
E2232 user protocol: What `debug adapter received an invalid protocol message`. Why `the DAP header or JSON body is malformed`, `request <command> is not legal while the session is <state>`, or `request sequence <seq> was duplicated or invalid`. Fix `restart the debug session; update the editor extension if the message repeats`.
E2233 tool timeout: What `debug operation <operation> did not finish within <duration>`. Why `the debugger engine stopped responding while the session was <state>`. Fix after proved restoration `retry <operation>; if it repeats, restart the debug session`; after unproved attached cleanup `check the target process before retrying; Jet could not prove detach completed`.
E2234 tool backend: What `native debugger stopped speaking Jet's supported protocol`. Why `the verified backend exited unexpectedly`, `the backend returned malformed or unsupported output`, or `the backend executable changed after verification`. Fix `restart jet debug; if it repeats, run jet doctor and report E2234 with the redacted audit`. Discovery remains E2205.
E2235 user map: What `debug map does not match the selected program`. Why `.jetmap is missing`, `.jetmap schema <found> is not supported by Jet <version>`, `.jetmap build id <map-id> does not match program build id <program-id>`, `source hash for <workspace-relative-file> changed after the debug build`, or `a requested Jet line has no stoppable mapped span`. Fix first four `run jet debug <file> again to rebuild both artifacts`; last `move the breakpoint to a Jet statement on a mapped line`.
E2236 user editor/config incorporates latest EDITOR artifact. What `Jet debug configuration is invalid`. Why/Fix pairs: `field <field> <constraint>` / `correct <field> in the editor's Jet debug configuration`; `no runnable Jet file is active` / `open a runnable .jet file or choose Jet: Debug package entry`; `package entry selection is ambiguous: <workspace-relative entries>` / `choose one package entry explicitly`; `Jet extension protocol <editor-version> is incompatible with Jet <jet-version>` / `update Jet and the Jet editor extension to compatible versions`; `the private editor bridge could not authenticate the installed extension` / `reinstall the Jet extension and restart the editor, then retry`; `target path cannot be represented by jet.editor.debug-targets/v1` / `move the Jet source to a UTF-8 path, then retry`.
E2237 tool lost session: What `debug session connection was lost`. Why `the editor, adapter, or debugger control channel closed while the target was <state>`. Fix after proved cleanup `start a new debug session`; unproved `check the target process before starting another session; Jet could not prove <terminate|detach|continue> completed`.
E2238 user stale object: What `debug view is from an earlier stop`. Why `frame, scope, or variable reference <id> expired when execution resumed`. Fix `refresh the editor's stack and variables after the next stop`.
E2239 internal: What `internal debugger error <incident-id>`. Why `Jet could not preserve its debugger invariant; this is a Jet bug, not a problem in your program`. Fix `restart without reusing the session; report <incident-id> and the redacted audit if it repeats`. Exit 101.

Retry semantics. `retryable` is a strict response-field boolean meaning the receiver may automatically repeat the request after receiving this DiagnosticRecord/ErrorResponse. Every emitted debugger diagnostic sets retryable=false. For timeout_read only, Jet may perform one internal identical replay before emitting any DiagnosticRecord or failure response, after proving the same held process and stop generation. It may emit an un-coded DAP progressUpdate `retrying timed-out read once` or equivalent terminal progress, but that progress is not a diagnostic, has no E-code/class/What/Why/Fix, and is absent in non-progress JSON mode. One original request permits at most one replay total; replay cannot recursively replay. Success yields the original request's single success response and no timeout diagnostic. Only a failed replay emits timeout_read with retryable=false. Retry after fixing/changing/choosing/approving/restarting is a new deliberate request, never retryable=true.

Option B/C complete closed reason registry. The following entries are the entire allowed set. Each terminal projection uses the canonical four-line frame above with the stated code/class/What/Why/Fix; there is no hidden table or fallback reason. B uses phase code; C always uses E2230. Every DAP ErrorResponse also carries the stated Jet code, class, reason, and retryable value.
launch_build — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `launch_build: the debug build failed with the Jet diagnostic above`; Fix `fix the earlier Jet diagnostic, then run jet debug <file> again`; retryable false; cleanup `kill only owned child and close owned pipes`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee not-started`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
program_drift — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `program_drift: the verified program disappeared or changed before launch`; Fix `run jet debug <file> again to rebuild and revalidate the program`; retryable false; cleanup `close owned build/adapter handles; no child exists`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee not-started`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
process_create — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `process_create: the operating system denied process creation`; Fix `allow this user to start the program, then retry`; retryable false; cleanup `close owned pipes and remove owned temporary artifacts`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee not-started`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
program_first_frame — class tool; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `program_first_frame: the program stopped before the debugger established its first Jet frame`; Fix `run jet debug <file> again; if it repeats, rerun with --audit <filename> and report E2230`; retryable false; cleanup `reap owned child and close backend`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee exited(real code)`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
map_missing — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `map_missing: .jetmap is missing`; Fix `run jet debug <file> again to rebuild both artifacts`; retryable false; cleanup `remove unverified breakpoints; no process effect`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee not-started`; DAP `jet.mapMismatch/22037`.
map_schema — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `map_schema: .jetmap schema <found> is not supported by Jet <version>`; Fix `run jet debug <file> again to rebuild both artifacts`; retryable false; cleanup `remove unverified breakpoints; no process effect`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee not-started`; DAP `jet.mapMismatch/22037`.
map_build — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `map_build: .jetmap build id <map-id> does not match program build id <program-id>`; Fix `run jet debug <file> again to rebuild both artifacts`; retryable false; cleanup `remove unverified breakpoints; no process effect`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee not-started`; DAP `jet.mapMismatch/22037`.
map_source — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `map_source: source hash for <workspace-relative-file> changed after the debug build`; Fix `run jet debug <file> again to rebuild both artifacts`; retryable false; cleanup `remove unverified breakpoints; no process effect`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee not-started`; DAP `jet.mapMismatch/22037`.
map_unmappable — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `map_unmappable: a requested Jet line has no stoppable mapped span`; Fix `move the breakpoint to a Jet statement on a mapped line`; retryable false; cleanup `remove only that unverified backend breakpoint`; lifecycle `setBreakpoints request succeeds, response entry stays in request order with verified=false, adapter/state/debuggee unchanged`; DAP `no ErrorResponse and no numeric error id; A Breakpoint.message is exactly E2235: no stoppable Jet statement at <workspace-relative-file>:<line>; B/C Breakpoint.message is exactly E2230: no stoppable Jet statement at <workspace-relative-file>:<line>`.
config_field — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `config_field: field <field> <constraint>`; Fix `correct <field> in the editor's Jet debug configuration`; retryable false; cleanup `no process effect`; lifecycle `request failed or pre-adapter exit1; adapter state unchanged/not-started`; DAP `jet.invalidArguments/22032 when adapter exists`.
config_no_target — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `config_no_target: no runnable Jet file is active`; Fix `open a runnable .jet file or choose Jet: Debug package entry`; retryable false; cleanup `no process effect`; lifecycle `pre-adapter exit1; adapter absent; debuggee not-started`; DAP `no DAP message`.
config_ambiguous — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `config_ambiguous: package entry selection is ambiguous: <workspace-relative entries>`; Fix `choose one package entry explicitly`; retryable false; cleanup `no process effect`; lifecycle `pre-adapter exit1; adapter absent; debuggee not-started`; DAP `no DAP message`.
config_version — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `config_version: Jet extension protocol <editor-version> is incompatible with Jet <jet-version>`; Fix `update Jet and the Jet editor extension to compatible versions`; retryable false; cleanup `close private bridge; no process effect`; lifecycle `pre-adapter exit1; adapter absent; debuggee not-started`; DAP `no DAP message`.
config_bridge_auth — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `config_bridge_auth: the private editor bridge could not authenticate the installed extension`; Fix `reinstall the Jet extension and restart the editor, then retry`; retryable false; cleanup `close every received handle and bridge; no process effect`; lifecycle `pre-adapter exit1; adapter absent; debuggee not-started`; DAP `no DAP message`.
config_path_encoding — class user; B terminal `E2230` What `debug setup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `config_path_encoding: target path cannot be represented by jet.editor.debug-targets/v1`; Fix `move the Jet source to a UTF-8 path, then retry`; retryable false; cleanup `close path handles; no process effect`; lifecycle `pre-adapter exit1; adapter absent; debuggee not-started`; DAP `no DAP message`.
attach_exit — class tool; B terminal `E2231` What `debug control failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `attach_exit: the verified process exited before attach completed`; Fix `choose the process again; Jet will revalidate identity and ask for new authority`; retryable false; cleanup `prove held target exited; release handle`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee exited(real code)`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
attach_permission — class tool; B terminal `E2231` What `debug control failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `attach_permission: the operating system revoked process-control permission`; Fix `choose the process again; Jet will revalidate identity and ask for new authority`; retryable false; cleanup `detach+continue temporary-stop target when applicable and prove it`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee detached-continued`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
attach_backend — class tool; B terminal `E2231` What `debug control failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `attach_backend: the debugger engine rejected the verified target`; Fix `choose the process again; Jet will revalidate identity and ask for new authority`; retryable false; cleanup `detach+continue and prove it; unproved becomes detach_unproved`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue; debuggee detached-continued`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
timeout_read — class tool; B terminal `E2231` What `debug control failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `timeout_read: idempotent read operation <operation> timed out twice while the session was <state>`; Fix `Jet already retried this read once; restart the debug session or reconnect the editor`; retryable false; cleanup `before replay, send one bounded cancel and prove the identical held process and stop generation`; lifecycle `before any DiagnosticRecord/failed response, replay the identical request once maximum; success gives one success response and no diagnostic; second timeout gives one failed response and leaves adapter at last proved state; debuggee unchanged`; DAP `jet.timeout/22035 only after the replay fails, with retryable=false`.
timeout_effect — class tool; B terminal `E2231` What `debug control failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `timeout_effect: effectful operation <operation> timed out while the session was <state>`; Fix `inspect the reported target state, then issue a new deliberate command`; retryable false; cleanup `send one bounded cancel and prove stopped, running, terminated, or detached state`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter last proved state or cleanup termination; debuggee proved state or unknown`; DAP `jet.timeout/22035`.
backend_exit — class tool; B terminal `E2231` What `debug control failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `backend_exit: the verified backend exited unexpectedly`; Fix `restart jet debug; if it repeats, run jet doctor and report the selected code with the redacted audit`; retryable false; cleanup `terminate owned child or detach+continue attached target and prove it`; lifecycle `request failed if correlatable; adapter exit1; debuggee terminated or detached-continued`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
backend_output — class tool; B terminal `E2231` What `debug control failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `backend_output: the backend returned malformed or unsupported output`; Fix `restart jet debug; if it repeats, run jet doctor and report the selected code with the redacted audit`; retryable false; cleanup `terminate/detach as backend_exit; never parse onward`; lifecycle `request failed if correlatable; adapter exit1; debuggee terminated or detached-continued`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
backend_drift — class tool; B terminal `E2231` What `debug control failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `backend_drift: the backend executable changed after verification`; Fix `restart jet debug; run jet doctor before retrying`; retryable false; cleanup `do not spawn changed backend; clean owned target/build state`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Initialized/continue before target, otherwise exit1 after cleanup`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034`.
stale_reference — class user; B terminal `E2231` What `debug control failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `stale_reference: frame, scope, or variable reference <id> expired when execution resumed`; Fix `refresh the editor's stack and variables after the next stop`; retryable false; cleanup `no cleanup; discard stale reference`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter Stopped/continue; debuggee stopped`; DAP `jet.staleReference/22036`.
malformed_frame — class user; B terminal `E2232` What `debug adapter received an invalid protocol message`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `malformed_frame: the DAP header or JSON body is malformed`; Fix `restart the debug session; update the editor extension if the message repeats`; retryable false; cleanup `apply disconnect defaults; prove terminate/detach when target exists`; lifecycle `no response when uncorrelatable; adapter exit1; debuggee per disconnect cleanup`; DAP `no correlatable DAP id`.
invalid_state — class user; B terminal `E2232` What `debug adapter received an invalid protocol message`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `invalid_state: request <command> is not legal while the session is <state>`; Fix `send the request only in the state named by the Jet debugger`; retryable false; cleanup `no cleanup; reject request`; lifecycle `request failed; adapter/state/debuggee unchanged`; DAP `jet.invalidState/22031`.
invalid_seq — class user; B terminal `E2232` What `debug adapter received an invalid protocol message`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `invalid_seq: request sequence <seq> was duplicated or invalid`; Fix `restart the debug session; update the editor extension if the message repeats`; retryable false; cleanup `no process effect while stream synchronization is proved; otherwise disconnect cleanup`; lifecycle `request failed and state unchanged if synchronized, else adapter exit1`; DAP `jet.invalidArguments/22032 when correlatable`.
lost_<state> — class tool; B terminal `E2233` What `debug cleanup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `lost_<state>: the editor, adapter, or debugger control channel closed while the target was <state>`; Fix `start a new debug session`; retryable false; cleanup `apply disconnect defaults and prove terminate or detach+continue`; lifecycle `no response if channel gone; adapter exit1; debuggee terminated or detached-continued`; DAP `console record then terminated only if channel survives; otherwise none`.
terminate_unproved — class tool; B terminal `E2233` What `debug cleanup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `terminate_unproved: Jet could not prove terminate completed`; Fix `check the target process before starting another session`; retryable false; cleanup `close owned control handles without claiming target death`; lifecycle `adapter exit1; debuggee unknown`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034 if correlatable`.
detach_unproved — class tool; B terminal `E2233` What `debug cleanup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `detach_unproved: Jet could not prove detach completed`; Fix `check the target process before retrying`; retryable false; cleanup `close control handles without claiming detach/continue`; lifecycle `adapter exit1; debuggee unknown`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034 if correlatable`.
continue_unproved — class tool; B terminal `E2233` What `debug cleanup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `continue_unproved: Jet could not prove continue completed`; Fix `check the target process before starting another session`; retryable false; cleanup `close control handles without claiming running state`; lifecycle `adapter exit1; debuggee unknown`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034 if correlatable`.
internal_invariant — class internal; B terminal `E2233` What `debug cleanup failed`; C terminal `E2230` What `debug operation failed`; Why `internal_invariant: Jet could not preserve its debugger invariant; this is a Jet bug, not a problem in your program`; Fix `restart without reusing the session; report <incident-id> and the redacted audit if it repeats`; retryable false; cleanup `perform fail-closed owned cleanup; never assert an unproved outcome`; lifecycle `request failure if correlatable; adapter exit101; debuggee proved cleanup state or unknown`; DAP `jet.unavailable/22034 if correlatable`.

B emits no E2234..E2239. C emits no E2231..E2239. Unknown reason is internal_invariant, never free-form text.

Option A DAP mapping and lifecycle, every code/variant. E2230 all variants -> jet.unavailable/22034, retryable false for every variant; launch failure response, owned child killed, adapter returns Initialized. E2231 all -> jet.unavailable/22034, retryable false even after verified detach+continue; attach failure response, adapter Initialized; unproved cleanup escalates E2237/E2239 and terminates adapter. E2232 malformed unsynchronized header/JSON -> no correlatable response and adapter exit 1; invalid_state -> jet.invalidState/22031, retryable false, state unchanged; invalid_seq -> jet.invalidArguments/22032, retryable false, stream remains only if synchronization is proved. E2233 -> jet.timeout/22035 only after timeout_read's one internal pre-response replay fails, or immediately for timeout_effect; every emitted response has retryable=false; proved restoration returns the failure response and keeps the adapter at its last proved usable state; only unproved cleanup escalates to E2237/E2239 and terminates the adapter. E2234 all -> jet.unavailable/22034, retryable false; fail response if correlation survives, launched child terminated or attached target detached+continued, exited/terminated events only when DAP1 lifecycle requires, adapter exits 1 after cleanup. E2235 missing/schema/build/source during launch -> jet.mapMismatch/22037, retryable false, response failure and Initialized; unmappable breakpoint -> setBreakpoints success with that breakpoint verified=false and exact Breakpoint.message `E2235: no stoppable Jet statement at <workspace-relative-file>:<line>`; no ErrorResponse/id, no session exit, state unchanged. E2236 all -> jet.invalidArguments/22032, retryable false; the stated Fix requires a new request, state unchanged; pre-adapter bridge/config failures have no DAP message and terminal/editor process exit 1. E2237 -> no response if channel is gone; if channel survives, console DiagnosticRecord then terminated, retryable false; adapter exit 1. E2238 -> jet.staleReference/22036, retryable false because refresh creates a new request/reference, request fails, session stays Stopped. E2239 -> jet.unavailable/22034 when correlatable, retryable false, terminated after fail-closed cleanup, adapter exit 101.

Inherited AUTH DAP mapping if AUTH later ratifies. E2240 is not an immediate failed launch: original launch/attach remains pending in AwaitingAuthority; approval continues that same request. User cancel -> jet.cancelled/22038, retryable false, one failure response, Initialized, adapter stays; expiry/broker loss -> jet.unavailable/22034, retryable false, Initialized. E2241 -> jet.unavailable/22034, retryable false; environment change/new approval creates a new request, original request fails, Initialized. E2242 -> jet.invalidArguments/22032, retryable false; path correction/new approval creates a new request, state unchanged/Initialized. E2243 -> jet.unavailable/22034, retryable false; new target verification creates a new request, attach request fails, Initialized with proved detach/continue. E2244 -> jet.unavailable/22034, retryable false; restoration/new session creates a new request; request fails, cleanup then Initialized or adapter exit 1 if backend lost. E2245 -> jet.unsupported/22033, retryable false until a remote decision changes capabilities; request fails, state unchanged.

Option B maps setup E2230 to 22032 for config reasons, 22037 for map reasons, otherwise 22034; control E2231 maps timeout reasons 22035, stale_reference 22036, others 22034; protocol E2232 maps as A; cleanup E2233 maps 22034 when correlatable and terminates. Option C maps its reason through the same semantic id; jetCode remains E2230. Thus every option preserves DAP id meaning rather than forcing one id per Jet code.

Request, process, and adapter outcomes are separate fields. DiagnosticRecord is `{schema:"jet.diagnostic/v1",code,class,severity:"error",what,why,fix,operation,reason?,retryable,requestOutcome,adapterOutcome,debuggeeOutcome,state,exit,source?,redactedDetails?}`. requestOutcome is failed/cancelled; adapterOutcome is continue/exit1/exit101; debuggeeOutcome is not-started/running/exited(code)/terminated/detached-continued/unknown. Terminal exit reflects its direct request; DAP response reflects request; exited/terminated reflect debuggee; adapter process exit reflects transport/internal lifecycle. Tests reject conflation.

E2203 collision migration and retirement. Live source uses E2203 both for interpreter debug boundary and Canvas unsafe-span extract; Canvas has no diagnostics-table ownership. Before debugger E2203 can retire, migrate Canvas atomically to E2935. E2935 What `Canvas extract cannot cross an unsafe source span`. Why `moving only part of an #Unsafe region could change its audited authority boundary`. Fix `select the whole #Unsafe region or extract code outside it`. Add diagnostics.md, jet explain, Canvas JSON/UI snapshot and update tests/canvas.rs in the same change; prove no E2203 remains in Canvas. Then, only after compatible NATIVE1 routing ships, remove debugger E2203 docs/explain/fixtures/tests and reserve E2203 forever. Until both gates finish, E2203 remains live and DIAG acceptance must fail.

Recovery common safety. Record last proved state and cleanup obligation. No blind retry. Launch kills only owned child. Attach follows AUTH held-identity detach/continue. Timeout sends one bounded cancel then proves state. Map mismatch never guesses. One internal pre-response replay is allowed once only for timeout_read with identical arguments, same held process, and same stop generation; no diagnostic exists before it and the emitted record after failure sets retryable=false. Never auto-retry launch, attach, resume, step, terminate, approval, evaluate, writes, stale references, or any request whose Fix requires change. Unproved cleanup becomes the selected option's cleanup/internal reason.

Acceptance is option-scoped. A snapshots every E2230..E2239 Why/Fix and mapping above. B snapshots every closed phase reason and confirms E2234..E2239 absent. C snapshots every closed umbrella reason and confirms E2231..E2239 absent. Every selected option adds diagnostics.md, jet explain, terminal TTY/plain/NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR, JSON schema/goldens, DAP response/event/lifecycle goldens, enabled-editor rendering, exit assertions, redaction, spans, hostile backend/path/secret fixtures, cleanup success/failure, and injected internal invariant. AUTH E2240..45 rows run only if live/open AUTH1 is ratified compatibly; until then they are gated and cannot be marked met. EDITOR-only E2236 rows run only if live/open EDITOR1 is ratified compatibly; until then they are gated and cannot be marked met. Dependency gates cannot be marked met early. NATIVE E2205/06 ownership is explicitly tested. E2203/E2935 migration order is tested.

Beginner pass: one plain What and one safe Fix; process state is never hidden behind editor jargon. Expert pass: code, class, reason, operation, retryability, request/adapter/debuggee outcomes, DAP id, state, redacted identities, and cleanup proof are inspectable. Hybrid pass: terminal, JSON, DAP, and enabled editors project the selected one diagnostic law.
decisions.story: Leah presses Debug on a native Jet service. Her backend is missing, then an old map is found, and later the editor loses the adapter while the process is paused. She needs one precise Jet explanation and safe next action each time—not LLDB text, a generic editor popup, or a false success. CI needs stable codes and exits; support needs redacted machine-readable facts.

decisions.detail:
Recommend A. One stable Jet code per recoverable debugger failure family, NATIVE and AUTH ownership preserved, one typed record translated across terminal, JSON, DAP, and editors, with proof-driven recovery and no blind retry. Users get a direct fix; automation branches on stable codes, classes, and exits without ever parsing backend text. B collapses those into four phase codes plus an enumerated reason field, so code-plus-reason searches still work but a bare code search loses the family; C uses one code for everything and cannot be distinguished by CI.

Tier compatibility (D-CANVAS-DEBUG-UX1). The axis here — code granularity — is independent of which engine ran. This one diagnostic law is the failure projection for both backends of the ratified tier-aware direction: a native lldb/DAP session for compiled runs and the in-tier session under `jet dev`. Tool-class native-backend failures (E2234 backend, E2231 attach-after-authority, and the E2205 tool-discovery boundary owned by NATIVE1) arise only for the compiled backend; the in-tier session emits only the tier-relevant subset — map, config, protocol, stale-reference, and internal-invariant families — through the identical four-line frame, ids, classes, and exit truth. The E2203 interpreter-boundary migration already recorded here is the same tier seam. No engine turns backend or editor prose into source truth, and no failure is ever reported as success.

Timeout-read replay happens internally before any diagnostic; an emitted timeout is final and retryable=false. Acceptance proves exactly two total backend attempts after a timeout. A replay path that makes a third attempt fails the test.

decisions.title: Build a jetdoc generator from the compiler semantic graph?
decisions.gist: Jet has doc comments (`///`, S49) and a live doctest mechanism (D-TEST4, implemented). The open question is whether to build `jet doc` — a tool that generates browsable API docs from parsed/type-resolved compiler output. Two sub-questions are entangled: (a) when does it ship relative to the sema index (D-SEMINDEX1/c96), and (b) what structured doc comment syntax does S49 need to add before generated docs are useful beyond a flat text dump? Doctests are already solved; this decision is about the API documentation generation surface only.
decisions.explainer: A semantic-graph doc generator reads the sema index (types, signatures, trait impls, doc comments) and emits HTML/Markdown API docs with tested examples. It is an E3 testing/docs ergonomics exit criterion. It depends on stable compiler seams (the `jet-sema` seam crate and the semantic index API card). Doctests close the loop: example code in `/// ` blocks is extracted and run as tests. Without this, doc quality decays because examples are untested. This card does not cover the LSP or IDE dossier views (those are D-DOSSIER1).
decisions.story: I publish a Jet library. I want `jet doc` to generate browsable API docs from my doc comments the same way `cargo doc` does — and I want any `/// ` example to fail CI if it stops compiling, not just silently rot.
decisions.detail: Adversarial pass (2026-06-28): (1) The inWild and Option A code use a pre-D-TEST4 doctest format; D-TEST4 is ratified — correct format is ```jet blocks with // => trailing comments. (2) Doctest execution (jet test --doctests) is already live via D-TEST4/c51; the open question is API doc generation only. (3) S49 says "plain text v1" — no structured doc section syntax is ratified; jetdoc built on this baseline can only emit a flat text dump. Either ratify S49 sections first or scope jetdoc explicitly to flat text. (4) Options A and C are functionally equivalent in sequencing (both gate on c96); the real decision is whether jetdoc is an E3 exit criterion.

options.name: Phase 1 AST doc now; Phase 2 sema-indexed when D-SEMINDEX1 lands (recommended)
options.detail: Phase 1 (Epoch 3, unblocked): a `jet doc` subcommand reads parsed public items and their raw `///` comments from the AST alone. Emits flat HTML per module: public signatures + doc text. No sema index required. Doctest execution (jet test --doctests) is already live via D-TEST4 — this adds browsable API surface only. Phase 2 (when D-SEMINDEX1/c96 is stable): upgrade to cross-linked, type-resolved, trait-impl-inclusive docs. Prerequisite before either phase: ratify S49 structured doc section syntax (currently "plain text v1") so Phase 1 emits structured sections instead of a raw text dump. Raise that as a follow-on ballot.

Doctests (D-TEST4) keep examples honest in the interim. Authors maintain hand-written Markdown. Viable internally but not for a public registry where doc quality is an ecosystem contract.

options.detail: No generated docs tool. Doctests still run (D-TEST4). No browsable API surface. Keeps toolchain surface smaller. Only viable for small internal libraries; not scalable as the registry grows.

decisions.title: Should Jet define a generic database driver interface with parameterized-queries-only enforcement?
decisions.gist: Jet already has SQLite support in core.db (c50). The question is whether to define a generic Driver trait that any database backend implements, with the interface enforcing parameterized queries only — making string-concatenated SQL structurally impossible. No generic driver interface exists today; this is the next step above the SQLite-specific API.
decisions.explainer: A Driver trait with a parameterized-only API eliminates SQL injection by construction — you cannot build a raw SQL string and execute it through the driver interface. This is a strong safety guarantee consistent with I1 (safe by default). The SQLite implementation (c50) becomes the first impl of Driver; Postgres, MySQL, and others would follow as stdlib or community packages. The interface design needs to cover: connection lifecycle, transactions (#Transact?), async vs sync, and error types. None of those require new syntax — they use existing Jet markers and the T ? E error type. The main risk is locking in a Driver shape before we know what async looks like in Jet; a sync-only v1 Driver is safe to ship now.
decisions.story: I want to write database code that works with SQLite in tests and Postgres in production, and I want the compiler to make it impossible to accidentally run string-interpolated SQL.

options.name: Define Driver trait + parameterized-only API; SQLite as first impl
options.detail: Specify a Driver trait with query(sql: &str, params: []Param) -> Result<Rows, DbError> and no raw-execute surface. SQLite (c50) is refactored to implement it. Safe by construction against SQL injection. Sync-only for now; async variant deferred until Jet's async story is settled.

options.name: Per-database APIs only; no generic Driver trait
options.detail: Keep core.db as the SQLite-specific API. Each new database gets its own module with its own API. No shared interface. Simpler short-term; loses the cross-backend portability and the injection guarantee at the interface level.

options.name: Defer — design after async story is settled
options.detail: The right Driver shape depends on whether queries are sync or async. Wait until Jet's async/concurrency model is ratified, then design Driver once with the right shape. Risk: blocks any new database backends in the meantime.

comparisons.note: Generic DB interface with parameterized queries via ? placeholders. Drivers register themselves. No string-building API at the interface level — close to what Jet is proposing.
Macro-verified parameterized queries checked against a live DB at compile time. Stronger than Go but requires a live DB in CI — Jet's approach is lighter.

decisions.title: Next-generation FFI: what one structure makes every foreign language near-trivial to wrap, replace in situ, and tap immediately?
decisions.gist: Pick the architecture every foreign language shares: per-language namespaces with pluggable binders, uniform extern blocks, typed projection importers, or runtime-broker sidecars.
decisions.explainer: Jet already speaks two foreign languages, each with its own shape: Rust via extern rust "crate@version" { … } (S50) and C via generated bindings mounted at c.<lib> with a user overlay (S59). JS is sequenced next, Swift later (D-JSWIFTFFI1). The owner's bar: using a library from almost any language should feel almost as easy as using a Jet package — every ecosystem's work immediately usable, and any foreign dependency replaceable later by a native Jet implementation without touching call sites (in-situ replacement). This ballot picks the one structure all languages share. How deep each language's binding goes (shallow declaration binding, full typed projection, or a runtime broker) is a per-language follow-up ballot on top of the winning frame — the frame is what must never vary.
decisions.story: Doris is building a lab-data tool in Jet. The only mature reader for her instrument's file format is a Python package; the best plotting library is on npm; a checksum routine she needs ships as a C header. She wants all three working this afternoon, each behind an ordinary typed Jet API with honest effects — and when a native Jet plotting package appears next year, she wants to swap it in by changing one dependency line, not rewriting call sites.
decisions.inWild:
use py.h5instrument as h5     // Python package, typed surface
use js.plotly as plot          // npm package (D-NPMTYPE1 stubs)
use "xxhash.h" as xx           // C header, script tier (S59)

fn main() #(Fs, Proc) {
    run := h5.read("run-0142.h5")
    print(xx.hash64(run.raw))
    plot.line(run.times, run.values)
}
decisions.detail: A, C, and D compose rather than exclude: A is the surface law (namespaces, three tiers, overlay, in-situ shadowing, lockfile provenance); C and D are per-language binder strategies BEHIND that surface — projection importers for static languages (C, Swift, Rust), a broker likely right for Python/JS dynamic tails, shallow declaration binding where that's enough. Ratifying A means: the surface ships now; follow-up ballots (D-FFI-PY1, D-FFI-JS1 folding in D-NPMTYPE1, D-FFI-SWIFT1 honoring D-JSWIFTFFI1 sequencing) pick each language's strategy on the common frame. Existing ratifications are preserved, not reopened: S59 is already the C instance of A; S50's extern rust block becomes the rust binder's declaration format inside rust.*; D-DEP1's vendoring/hash-pinning law extends to every language's refs. I8: one FFI structure for all languages is the point — shipping B alongside A would be two spellings for one job. I1/I2 hold in every option: user code is safe unless #Unsafe; no foreign toolchain's errors ever reach the user unlaundered — binder diagnostics are Jet diagnostics with codes and snapshots (I4). Recommendation rationale: A is the only option that is uniform (one structure to learn), immediate (a new language needs only a binder, at whatever depth exists first), deep where it counts (projection strategy per language later), and structurally in-situ-replaceable — rank on beginner experience, one-path, and long-term correctness.

options.name: Language namespaces + pluggable binders (recommended)
options.detail: Generalize S59's proven C structure into the law for every language. Each foreign world mounts as a namespace <lang>.<lib> with the same three tiers everywhere: script tier (use "xxhash.h" as xx — bind on first compile), project tier (use py.h5instrument as h5 with the dep pinned in pkg.jet), overlay tier (#Extern module py.h5instrument { … } to refine generated types; overlay wins). `jet bind <lang>` is a per-language binder producing inspectable, committable bindings in .jet/bindings/<lang>/<lib>.jet. Safety: generated bindings are safe wrappers by construction (marshaling internals compiler-vetted like std internals — I1); calling a foreign symbol outside a binding requires #Unsafe("reason"). In-situ replacement is structural: any <lang>.<lib> can be shadowed by a Jet package exporting the same surface — call sites never change. Per-language depth (projection vs broker vs shallow) is chosen behind this surface, one follow-up ballot per language.

options.name: Uniform extern blocks (generalize S50)
options.detail: Every language uses S50's declaration-first shape: extern <lang> "ref@version" { fn … = "path" }. Maximal explicitness — every crossing is written in the file — and one grammar for all languages. The cost is the wall: wrapping a real library means hundreds of declaration lines per library (generated or not, they live in your project), there is no namespace to shadow so in-situ replacement means hand-built wrapper modules, and 'almost trivial' is exactly what it isn't.

options.name: Typed projection importers only
options.detail: Every language gets a full compiler importer (Swift-Clang-importer style): use py.h5instrument elaborates the package's surface — from type stubs and introspection — directly into checked Jet types with effects and ownership mapped; overlays refine (raw pointer -> checked handle). The deepest 'feels native' ceiling, and the right end-state for static languages. As the only mechanism, it makes every new language wait for a full importer before ANY access exists — the opposite of tapping ecosystems immediately.

options.name: Runtime broker sidecars only
options.detail: Foreign runtimes run as supervised sidecar processes with a typed message boundary; py.* calls marshal to a Python worker (Mojo's play). Any language with a runtime works day one and effects are honest (#(Proc) on every call) — but values are serialized at every crossing (no zero-copy, no shared memory), C headers and Rust crates don't fit the model at all, and production binaries grow a process tree. Right as a per-language strategy for dynamic tails; wrong as the only structure.

comparisons.note: @cImport makes C trivial — but only C. The lesson: binder-in-the-compiler is magic; the miss: no structure for a second language.
Clang importer: full typed projection of C/ObjC — foreign APIs feel native. The depth ceiling to aim per-language binders at.
comparisons.code: import Accelerate   // C library, arrives as typed Swift

comparisons.note: Imports any Python module day one via a runtime broker — instant ecosystem reach, marshaled boundary. The play for dynamic-language tails.
comparisons.code:
from python import Python
let np = Python.import_module("numpy")

comparisons.note: P/Invoke plus WinRT projections: two tiers under one runtime — proof that shallow decls and deep projections coexist behind one surface.
Polyglot: many languages, one VM — reach bought with total runtime lock-in; the anti-goal for an AOT language.

decisions.title: Python binder depth: how deep does `use py.<lib>` reach into CPython?
decisions.gist: The D-FFI-UNIFY1 frame is law; this picks Python's binder strategy behind it. Python's ecosystem is C-extension-heavy (numpy, torch), so the binder must reach real CPython. Choose the host model: crash-isolated sidecar broker, in-process libpython embed, Python-on-WASM, or a shallow script shim.
decisions.explainer: The owner's bar (card #180) is tapping any ecosystem immediately. Python is the biggest prize and the hardest: its value lives in native C-extension packages, so a pure reimplementation or a WASM-only path forfeits most of the ecosystem. Two real hosts remain: an in-process libpython embed (zero-copy on buffer-protocol arrays, but a buggy native extension can take the whole process down and the GIL must be managed) and a supervised sidecar worker (a crashing extension dies with the worker, honest #(Proc)-style effect, but values marshal across a process boundary — no zero-copy of large tensors). Under I1, crash containment argues for the broker as the safe default; the embed is the expert performance tier for hot numeric paths, mirroring how D-PLUGIN1 made the WASM sandbox the default and native the opt-in. One `use py.X` surface either way; the host tier never moves call sites. Adds a `#(Py)` effect to the D-EFF4 set (owner-visible).
decisions.story: Doris is building a lab-data tool. The only mature reader for her instrument's file format is a Python package, and numpy is her numeric stack. She wants both working this afternoon behind an ordinary typed Jet API with honest effects — and she does not want a segfault in someone's C extension to take down her whole program.
decisions.detail: All options honor D-FFI-UNIFY1: `<lang>.<lib>` namespace, three tiers, `jet bind py` emitting inspectable `.jet/bindings/py/<lib>.jet`, safe wrappers by construction, `#Unsafe` only to reach a raw symbol outside a binding. The choice is only the host/depth. Marshalling law (all options): scalars<->Int/Float/Bool, str<->String, bytes/buffer-protocol arrays<->[T] or zero-copy View<T> in embed / copied in broker, dict<->struct or Map, list/tuple<->[T], None<->optional, Python exception->Jet Result + E-code (never a raw traceback). Async: asyncio coroutine -> Jet async task. Distribution: PyPI ref pinned in pkg.jet, wheel fetched + vendored + hash-pinned (D-DEP1); the CPython interpreter/libpython is a native runtime dep provisioned by jetpack/nixpkgs (ballot D-DEP-PY1). I1/I2/I4 hold in every option.

options.name: Sidecar-broker default + opt-in embed tier (recommended)
options.detail: The default host is a supervised CPython worker process (reuse the jetpack `services` supervision seam) with a typed message boundary — a crashing native extension takes down the worker, not your program, and the compiler restarts it. `#(Py)` effect on every call. An opt-in `py@embed` (dep flag or `#Embed` marker on the import) switches to in-process libpython for zero-copy on buffer-protocol arrays, for hot numeric paths. One `use py.X` surface; the tier is a distribution/perf choice, never a call-site change. Mirrors D-PLUGIN1's sandbox-default / native-opt-in shape.

options.name: Sidecar broker only
options.detail: Every py.* call marshals to a supervised worker; no in-process path ever. Maximum crash isolation and the simplest safety story; large arrays always copy across the process boundary, so a tensor-heavy inner loop pays a serialization cost with no escape hatch.

options.name: In-process libpython embed only
options.detail: Every py.* call runs in-process against linked libpython, GIL-scoped, zero-copy on buffer-protocol types. Fastest and simplest to reason about for numeric code; a faulty native extension segfaults the host process (weaker isolation), which sits uneasily with I1's crash-containment posture as an unconditional default.

options.name: Python-on-WASM sandbox
options.detail: Run CPython compiled to WASM (Pyodide/CPython-wasi) on the already-approved wasmtime runtime. Fully sandboxed and I1-clean by construction, and reuses the #5 runtime — but the C-extension long tail (arbitrary wheels, native torch) does not run under it, so it forfeits the exact packages that make Python worth calling. Right as a niche isolation tier, wrong as the reach story.
options.code: use py.pure_python_lib as p        // sandboxed; native wheels unavailable

options.name: Subprocess script shim (shallow)
options.detail: `jet bind py` emits thin declarations that shell out to `python -c`/script invocations per call. Trivial to stand up; no persistent interpreter, so state does not carry between calls, everything re-imports each time, and rich values degrade to stringly-typed exchange. Below the frame's typed-surface bar.
options.code: use py.h5instrument as h5          // each call = a fresh python process

comparisons.note: Imports any Python module day one via an in-process CPython embed — the reach bar to match. Mojo accepts the embed's coupling; Jet's I1 posture pushes the safe default toward isolation with embed as the opt-in.
comparisons.code:
from python import Python
let np = Python.import_module("numpy")

comparisons.note: In-process libpython with GIL tokens and typed conversions — the mechanism the embed tier wraps. Shows zero-copy buffer-protocol bridging is a solved shape.
Out-of-process typed boundary with supervision — the broker model. Proven isolation; the cost is marshaling, which is why large-array paths want the embed escape hatch.

decisions.recommendation: A

decisions.title: Approve a CPython runtime dependency for the Python binder
decisions.gist: The Python binder needs a real CPython interpreter — libpython linked in-process (embed tier) and/or a CPython executable for the sidecar worker. That is a new runtime-side external dependency, an I6 owner decision, exactly parallel to D-DEP-WASM1 for wasmtime.
decisions.explainer: I6 keeps the compiler (Source/) zero-external-crate forever and requires owner approval for any new stdlib/runtime external dependency. D-FFI-PY1's reach depends on real CPython: the sidecar broker needs a CPython executable present, and the embed tier links libpython. This is runtime-side only — never in Source/ — mirroring how D-DEP-WASM1=A approved wasmtime for plugins. The dependency is provisioned per the ratified native-deps policy (nixpkgs interim, jetpack core provider long-term), carries a native-ize obligation (the frozen end-state), and is hash-pinned in .jet/lock. Without this approval the Python binder cannot ship at any depth except the WASM-sandbox tier (which forfeits the C-extension ecosystem).
decisions.story: The build needs numpy to actually run. That means a CPython the compiler can drive — linked or spawned. Before any code assumes libpython is on the link line, the owner decides whether Jet takes that runtime dependency and how it is provisioned.
decisions.detail: Runtime-side only (I6 holds — never in Source/). Provisioning follows the ratified native-deps policy: nixpkgs where the user has Nix, jetpack core provider long-term, with a clear message on machines lacking both. Native-ize obligation recorded (parallel to D-DEP-WASM1's frozen own-runtime end-state). Hash-pinned in .jet/lock (D-DEP1). Only pulled in when a project actually uses py.* — a pure-Jet project never acquires it.

options.name: Approve CPython runtime dep (libpython embed + broker interpreter), provisioned via nixpkgs/jetpack (recommended)
options.detail: Sanction CPython as a runtime-side dependency for the Python binder: libpython on the link line for the embed tier, a CPython executable for the sidecar worker. Never in Source/ (I6 holds). Provisioned by nixpkgs (interim) / jetpack core provider (long-term); hash-pinned; native-ize obligation recorded; acquired only when a project uses py.*. This is the D-DEP-WASM1 precedent applied to Python and unblocks D-FFI-PY1 at full depth.
options.code:
deps: { numpy: py@">=1.26" }   // pulls the approved CPython runtime
// pure-Jet projects never acquire it

options.name: Broker interpreter only (no libpython linkage)
options.detail: Approve only a CPython executable for the sidecar worker; never link libpython. Keeps the dependency at arm's length (out-of-process only) and avoids in-process linkage entirely; forecloses the zero-copy embed tier of D-FFI-PY1, so large-array numeric paths always marshal.
options.code: deps: { numpy: py@">=1.26" }   // worker process only; no embed tier

options.name: No CPython dep — WASM-sandbox Python only
options.detail: Decline the CPython runtime dependency; the Python binder is limited to the Python-on-WASM tier on the existing wasmtime. No new dep at all, fully sandboxed — but the native C-extension ecosystem (numpy/scipy/torch) does not run, gutting the reason to call Python.
options.code: use py.pure_python_lib as p    // native wheels unavailable

comparisons.note: The exact precedent: a runtime-side external dep approved for a capability (plugins), never in Source/, hash-pinned, native-ize obligation. Option A is the same shape for Python.
